short_description.id: Yalmavuz (Yalmauz) adalah iblis jahat dalam mitologi Bashkir dan makhluk raksasa berkepala banyak dalam mitologi Turkik dan Altai.
short_description.en: Yalmavuz (Yalmauz) is an evil demon of Bashkir mythology and a many-headed giant being of Turkic and Altai mythology.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Bashkir, Yalmauz adalah iblis jahat yang namanya berarti "yang menelan segalanya", dari kata ialmau, "melingkupi", dan auyz, "mulut". Ia muncul dalam dongeng Bashkir seperti Karasa-batyr dan Altyndugha-batyr. Iblis ini berupa makhluk mirip ular berkepala tujuh, sembilan, atau dua belas yang tinggal di kebun yang ditanaminya sendiri; dalam dongeng, para batyr menyelamatkan gadis-gadis tawanannya dengan bertarung dan membunuhnya.
long_description.en: In Bashkir mythology Yalmauz is an evil demon whose name means "the one who swallows everything", from ialmau, "to enclose", and auyz, "mouth". It appears in Bashkir tales such as Karasa-batyr and Altyndugha-batyr. The demon is a serpent-like creature with seven, nine or twelve heads living in a garden it planted itself; in the tales, heroes (batyrs) free the maidens it holds captive by fighting and killing it.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan, Yalmauz juga penyihir pemakan manusia, vampir yang menculik bayi dan gadis; M. A. Kulaev menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan tua bermulut lebar. Dalam bahasa Uighur kata yalmauz berarti "naga". Dalam mitologi Turkik dan Altai, Yalmavuz adalah raksasa berwujud manusia dengan tiga, tujuh, atau dua belas kepala, berwarna hitam atau kuning, memusuhi kuda, dan memakan manusia.
long_description.en: By belief Yalmauz is also a man-eating sorcerer, a vampire that abducts babies and girls; M. A. Kulaev describes it as a wide-mouthed old woman. In Uyghur, yalmauz means "dragon". In Turkic and Altai mythology Yalmavuz is a human-shaped giant with three, seven or twelve heads, black or yellow in colour, hostile to horses and devouring people.

short_description.id: Yel iyesi adalah roh angin dalam mitologi Turk, Tatar, dan Altai; di sumber lain digambarkan sebagai roh perempuan mirip peri yang dapat membentuk hembusan angin dengan suaranya.
short_description.en: Yel iyesi is the wind spirit of Turkic, Tatar and Altai mythology, described elsewhere as a female fairy-like spirit whose voice can form gusts of wind.

long_description.id: Yel iyesi adalah roh atau dewa angin dalam tradisi Turkik. Sumber kedua menyebutnya roh angin dalam mitologi Turk, Tatar, dan Altai, sedangkan sumber ketiga menyebutnya roh pelindung angin dan menegaskan bahwa setiap angin punya iyesi-nya sendiri.
long_description.en: The Yel iyesi is the spirit or deity of wind in Turkic tradition. The second source calls it the wind spirit in Turk, Tatar and Altai mythology, while the third calls it the protective spirit of the wind and adds that every wind has its own iye.

long_description.id: Menurut artikel pertama, Yel İye adalah roh perempuan mirip peri yang tinggal di alam liar dan kadang di awan. Mereka biasanya tampil sebagai gadis cantik, telanjang atau berbusana putih berkilau. Suara mereka sangat indah dan dapat membentuk hembusan angin besar yang mampu mengangkat rumah ke udara.
long_description.en: According to the first article, the Yel İye are female fairy-like spirits living in the wilderness and sometimes in the clouds. They usually appear as beautiful maidens, naked or in sparkling white dresses. Their voices are very beautiful and can form large gusts of wind able to lift houses into the air.

long_description.id: Mereka juga disebut pejuang garang yang membuat bumi bergetar ketika bertempur, memiliki kekuatan penyembuhan dan ramalan, serta kadang bersedia menolong manusia. Konon bila sehelai rambut Yel İyesi dicabut ia akan mati atau terpaksa kembali ke wujud aslinya, dan manusia dapat menguasainya dengan mencuri rambut itu.
long_description.en: They are also called fierce warriors who make the earth shake when they do battle, with healing and prophetic powers, and they are sometimes willing to help human beings. It is said that if a hair of the Yel İyesi is plucked she will die or be forced back into her true shape, and a human may gain control of her by stealing that hair.

long_description.id: Dalam budaya Azeri, nama Haydar diberikan kepada Yel İyesi, dan orang memanggilnya saat menampi gandum. Sumber ketiga mencatat bahwa memanggil roh pelindung dengan berteriak umumnya dianggap tidak hormat dan berbahaya, tetapi Yel iyesi adalah pengecualiannya.
long_description.en: In Azeri culture the name Haydar is given to the Yel İyesi, and people call on it when winnowing grain. The third source notes that shouting for protective spirits is generally seen as disrespectful and dangerous, with the Yel iyesi as the exception.

literal_meaning.id: Akar kata ini berarti angin atau hembusan, dan juga membawa makna jiwa, roh, dan jin.
literal_meaning.en: The root means wind or breeze and also carries the meanings of life, spirit and jinn.

short_description.id: Yemaja (Yemọja) adalah dewi air utama dalam agama Yoruba, pelindung sungai, khususnya Sungai Ogun di Nigeria, yang di Brasil dan Kuba dipuja terutama sebagai dewi laut.
short_description.en: Yemaja (Yemọja) is a leading water goddess of the Yoruba religion and guardian of rivers, above all the Ogun River in Nigeria; in Brazil and Cuba she is honoured chiefly as a goddess of the sea.

long_description.id: Yemọja, yang juga ditulis Yemaja, Yemanjá, atau Yemayá, adalah salah satu dewi air terpenting dalam agama Yoruba. Sebagai seorang oriṣa, ia menjadi pelindung sungai, terutama Sungai Ogun di Nigeria. Di Yorubaland peran dewa laut dipegang Olókun, sementara Yemọja memimpin para dewi sungai lainnya.
long_description.en: Yemọja, whose name is also spelled Yemaja, Yemanjá or Yemayá, ranks among the chief water deities of Yoruba religion. As an oriṣa she watches over rivers, the Ogun River of Nigeria in particular. Within Yorubaland the sea belongs to Olókun, and Yemọja stands at the head of the remaining river goddesses.

long_description.id: Ia digambarkan keibuan dan sangat melindungi: ia menghibur anak-anaknya dan menghapus duka mereka, serta dikatakan mampu menyembuhkan kemandulan. Ia jarang marah, tetapi amarahnya bisa merusak seperti banjir sungai yang bergolak. Sebagian pendetanya percaya bahwa air tawarnya membantu Ọbàtálá membentuk manusia dari tanah liat.
long_description.en: She is pictured as a caring, fiercely protective mother who consoles her children and washes away their grief, and she is credited with curing infertility. Her temper is slow to rise, yet once roused it can wreck like a swollen, raging river. Some of her priests hold that her fresh water helped Ọbàtálá shape people from clay.

long_description.id: Namanya dijelaskan sebagai gabungan kata Yoruba untuk ibu, anak, dan ikan. Banyak pemuja menggambarkannya sebagai putri duyung, dan atributnya mencakup ikan serta cermin tangan bernama Abebê. Cangkang kauri melambangkan kekayaannya.
long_description.en: Her name is explained as a blend of the Yoruba words for mother, child and fish. Many devotees portray her as a mermaid, and her attributes include fish and a hand mirror called Abebê. Cowrie shells stand for her wealth.

long_description.id: Praktik menyamakannya dengan figur Perawan Maria, misalnya Our Lady of Regla, muncul pada masa perdagangan budak Trans-Atlantik. Di Brasil dan Kuba ia menjadi dewi laut, dan di Kuba ia dianggap salah satu orisha terpenting: dalam Candomblé dan Umbanda ia adalah Ratu Samudra dan pelindung nelayan, sedangkan dalam Santería ia adalah ibu segala makhluk hidup dan pemilik lautan. Setiap 2 Februari ribuan orang membawa persembahan ke tempat sucinya di Rio Vermelho.
long_description.en: Identifying her with Virgin Mary figures such as Our Lady of Regla became a practice in the era of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade. In Brazil and Cuba she became a sea goddess, counted in Cuba among the most important orishas: Candomblé and Umbanda honour her as Queen of the Ocean and patron of fishermen, while in Santería she is mother of every living being and owner of the seas. On each February 2 thousands bring offerings to her shrine in Rio Vermelho.

long_description.id: Kisah tentang pasangannya berbeda-beda. Satu legenda menyebut ia menikah dengan Oxalá dan menjadi penjaga kepala setelah menyembuhkan suaminya, sedangkan artikel ketiga menyebut suaminya Aganju. Kisah lain menyatakan ia selalu ada dan semua kehidupan, termasuk para orisha, lahir darinya.
long_description.en: Accounts of her spouse vary. One legend weds her to Oxalá and makes her guardian of heads after she cures him, whereas the third article names Aganju as her husband. Still other stories hold that she has always existed and that all life, the orishas included, came from her.

claims.quote: Yemọja (also: Yemaja, Yemanjá, Yemoyá, Yemayá; there are many different transliterations in other languages) is a major water deity in the Yoruba religion.

statement.id: Yemọja (juga Yemaja, Yemanjá, Yemoyá, Yemayá) adalah dewi air utama dalam agama Yoruba.
statement.en: Yemọja (also Yemaja, Yemanjá, Yemoyá, Yemayá) is a major water deity in the Yoruba religion.

claims.quote: She is an oriṣa, and the patron spirit of rivers, particularly the Ogun River in Nigeria, and of oceans in Cuban and Brazilian Orisha religions.

statement.id: Ia adalah seorang oriṣa, roh pelindung sungai, terutama Sungai Ogun di Nigeria, dan roh pelindung samudra dalam agama Orisha di Kuba (Cuban) dan Brasil (Brazilian).
statement.en: She is an oriṣa and patron spirit of rivers, especially the Ogun River in Nigeria, and of oceans in Cuban and Brazilian Orisha religions.

claims.quote: She is often syncretized with either Our Lady of Regla in the Afro-Cuban diaspora or various other Virgin Mary figures of the Catholic Church, a practice that emerged during the era of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade.

statement.id: Ia sering disinkretiskan dengan Our Lady of Regla dalam diaspora Afro-Kuba atau dengan figur Perawan Maria (Virgin Mary) lain dari Gereja Katolik, praktik yang muncul pada masa perdagangan budak Trans-Atlantik.
statement.en: She is often syncretized with Our Lady of Regla in the Afro-Cuban diaspora or other Virgin Mary figures of the Catholic Church, a practice that emerged in the era of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade.

claims.quote: Yemọja is said to be motherly and strongly protective, and to care deeply for all her children, comforting them and cleansing them of sorrow.

statement.id: Yemọja dikatakan bersifat keibuan dan sangat melindungi, sangat peduli pada semua anaknya, menghibur mereka dan membersihkan mereka dari duka.
statement.en: Yemọja is said to be motherly and strongly protective, caring deeply for all her children, comforting them and cleansing them of sorrow.

claims.quote: She does not easily lose her temper, but when angered she can be quite destructive and violent, as the flood waters of turbulent rivers.

statement.id: Ia tidak mudah marah, tetapi bila marah ia bisa sangat merusak dan keras, seperti air bah sungai yang bergolak.
statement.en: She does not easily lose her temper, but when angered she can be destructive and violent, like the flood waters of turbulent rivers.

claims.quote: Some of the priests of Yemọja believe that she used her fresh water to help Ọbàtálá in the molding of human beings out of clay.

statement.id: Sebagian pendeta Yemọja percaya bahwa ia memakai air tawarnya untuk membantu Ọbàtálá membentuk manusia dari tanah liat.
statement.en: Some priests of Yemọja believe she used her fresh water to help Ọbàtálá mould human beings out of clay.

claims.quote: Yemọja is often depicted as a mermaid by a number of devotees, and is associated with water, feminine mysteries, and the moon in some diaspora communities.

statement.id: Yemọja sering digambarkan sebagai putri duyung (mermaid) oleh sejumlah pemuja, dan di beberapa komunitas diaspora dikaitkan dengan air, misteri feminin, dan bulan.
statement.en: Yemọja is often depicted as a mermaid by devotees and, in some diaspora communities, is associated with water, feminine mysteries and the moon.

claims.quote: She is said to be able to cure infertility in women, and cowrie shells represent her wealth.

statement.id: Ia dikatakan mampu menyembuhkan kemandulan pada perempuan, dan cangkang kauri (cowrie) melambangkan kekayaannya.
statement.en: She is said to be able to cure infertility in women, and cowrie shells represent her wealth.

claims.quote: Her name is a contraction of the Yoruba words Iye, a dialect variant of "ìyá" meaning "mother"; ọmọ, meaning "child"; and ẹja, meaning "fish"

statement.id: Namanya adalah singkatan kata-kata Yoruba Iye (ìyá, ibu), ọmọ (anak), dan ẹja (ikan).
statement.en: Her name is a contraction of the Yoruba words Iye (ìyá, mother), ọmọ (child) and ẹja (fish).

claims.quote: In West Africa, Yemọja is worshipped as a high-ranking river deity, but in Brazil and Cuba she is worshipped mainly as a sea/ocean deity.

statement.id: Di Afrika Barat (West Africa) Yemọja dipuja sebagai dewi sungai berkedudukan tinggi, tetapi di Brasil (Brazil) dan Kuba (Cuba) ia terutama dipuja sebagai dewi laut.
statement.en: In West Africa Yemọja is worshipped as a high-ranking river deity, but in Brazil and Cuba mainly as a sea or ocean deity.

claims.quote: It is Olókun that fills the role of sea deity in Yorubaland, while Yemọja is a leader of the other river deities.

statement.id: Di Yorubaland, Olókun yang berperan sebagai dewa laut, sedangkan Yemọja adalah pemimpin para dewi sungai lainnya.
statement.en: In Yorubaland it is Olókun who fills the role of sea deity, while Yemọja leads the other river deities.

claims.quote: She is the Queen of the Ocean, the patron spirit of the fishermen and the survivors of shipwrecks, the feminine principle of creation, and the spirit of moonlight.

statement.id: Dalam Candomblé dan Umbanda ia adalah Ratu Samudra (Queen of the Ocean), pelindung nelayan dan penyintas kapal karam, prinsip feminin penciptaan, serta roh cahaya bulan.
statement.en: In Candomblé and Umbanda she is the Queen of the Ocean, patron of fishermen and shipwreck survivors, the feminine principle of creation and the spirit of moonlight.

claims.quote: In Candomblé and Umbanda, Yemanjá is one of the seven Orixás.

statement.id: Dalam Candomblé dan Umbanda, Yemanjá adalah salah satu dari tujuh Orixá.
statement.en: In Candomblé and Umbanda, Yemanjá is one of the seven Orixás.

claims.quote: Every February 2, thousands of people line up at dawn to leave their offerings at her shrine in Rio Vermelho.

statement.id: Setiap 2 Februari (February 2), ribuan orang antre sejak fajar untuk meninggalkan persembahan di tempat sucinya di Rio Vermelho.
statement.en: Every February 2, thousands of people line up at dawn to leave offerings at her shrine in Rio Vermelho.

claims.quote: In Santería or regla de ocha, Yemayá is the mother of all living things as well as the owner of the oceans and seas.

statement.id: Dalam Santería atau regla de ocha, Yemayá adalah ibu segala makhluk hidup sekaligus pemilik samudra dan lautan.
statement.en: In Santería or regla de ocha, Yemayá is the mother of all living things and the owner of the oceans and seas.

claims.quote: Sie wird daher häufig als Wasserfrau dargestellt und repräsentiert z. B. in Brasilien das Salzwasser des Meeres, in Nigeria ist sie eine Flussgöttin im Bundesstaat Ogun.

statement.id: Ia sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan air (Wasserfrau); di Brasil (Brasilien) ia mewakili air asin laut, sedangkan di Nigeria ia adalah dewi sungai di negara bagian Ogun.
statement.en: She is often shown as a water woman (Wasserfrau); in Brazil (Brasilien) she represents the salt water of the sea, while in Nigeria she is a river goddess in Ogun State.

claims.quote: Yemayá ist verheiratet mit Oxalá. Da sie so viel mit ihrem Mann redete, wurde er verrückt. ... Yemayá musste ihn heilen und wurde so zur Hüterin der Köpfe.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, Yemayá menikah (verheiratet) dengan Oxalá; karena ia terlalu banyak bicara, suaminya menjadi gila, lalu Yemayá harus menyembuhkannya dan dengan itu menjadi penjaga kepala (Hüterin der Köpfe).
statement.en: In legend Yemayá is married (verheiratet) to Oxalá; because she talked so much he went mad, and Yemayá had to heal him, thereby becoming guardian of heads (Hüterin der Köpfe).

claims.quote: Ihre Attribute sind Fische und ein Handspiegel namens Abebê. Ihr Wochentag ist der Samstag.

statement.id: Atributnya adalah ikan (Fische) dan cermin tangan bernama Abebê; hari sucinya adalah Sabtu (Samstag).
statement.en: Her attributes are fish (Fische) and a hand mirror called Abebê; her weekday is Saturday (Samstag).

claims.quote: Yemayá gilt als eine der wichtigsten Orishas auf Kuba.

statement.id: Yemayá dianggap salah satu orisha terpenting (wichtigsten Orishas) di Kuba.
statement.en: Yemayá is regarded as one of the most important orishas (wichtigsten Orishas) in Cuba.

claims.quote: Il existe de nombreuses histoires contant la façon dont elle est devenue la mère de tous les esprits. Elle était mariée à Aganju
claims.locator: En Afrique, dans les traditions yoruba

statement.id: Artikel ketiga menyebut banyak kisah tentang bagaimana ia menjadi ibu semua roh (mère de tous les esprits), dan menyatakan ia menikah (mariée) dengan Aganju.
statement.en: The third article says many stories tell how she became mother of all spirits (mère de tous les esprits), and states she was married (mariée) to Aganju.

claims.quote: D'autres histoires racontent que Yemaya a toujours existé et que toute vie est née d'elle, y compris tous les orishas.
claims.locator: En Afrique, dans les traditions yoruba

statement.id: Kisah lain (D'autres histoires) menyebut Yemaya selalu ada dan semua kehidupan lahir darinya, termasuk semua orisha.
statement.en: Other stories (D'autres histoires) say Yemaya has always existed and all life, including all the orishas, was born from her.

summary.en: She is married to Oxalá.

summary.id: Ia menikah dengan Aganju.
summary.en: She was married to Aganju.

short_description.id: Zhuque atau Burung Merah adalah salah satu Empat Lambang rasi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Zhuque, the Vermilion Bird, belongs to the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations.

long_description.id: Zhuque atau Burung Merah adalah salah satu Empat Lambang rasi Tiongkok. Dalam sistem lima unsur, ia mewakili api, selatan, dan musim panas.
long_description.en: Zhuque, the Vermilion Bird, belongs to the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations. In the five-phase system, it corresponds to fire, south, and summer.

long_description.id: Burung Merah merupakan roh rasi yang berbeda dari fenghuang. Tujuh kedudukan bulan dikelompokkan dalam wilayah rasi Burung Merah.
long_description.en: The Vermilion Bird is a constellation spirit distinct from fenghuang. Seven lunar mansions are grouped within its constellation region.

long_description.id: Teks-teks klasik Tiongkok menyebut Burung Merah dengan nama Zhuniao (朱鳥). Liji menempatkannya di depan saat berjalan, dengan Xuanwu di belakang, Naga Biru di kiri, dan Harimau Putih di kanan. Huainanzi mengaitkan selatan, api, dan musim panas dengan binatang Zhuniao, dan menyebut Taiwei menguasai Zhuque. Komentar atas Shiji menyebut bintang Liu sebagai paruh Zhuniao dan mengutip Wenyaogou yang menyebut esensi Kaisar Merah dari Istana Selatan adalah Zhuniao.
long_description.en: Classical Chinese texts call the Vermilion Bird Zhuniao (朱鳥). The Liji places it in front on the march, with Xuanwu behind, the Azure Dragon on the left and the White Tiger on the right. The Huainanzi associates the south, fire and summer with the Zhuniao beast, and says Taiwei governs Zhuque. short_description.id: Abzar iyesi adalah roh pelindung halaman, kandang, dan istal dalam cerita rakyat Turkik, yang bisa menyayangi atau mencelakai ternak.
short_description.en: Abzar iyesi is the protector spirit of the courtyard, cattle shed and stable in Turkic folklore, who may cherish or harm livestock.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Turkik, Abzar iyesi adalah roh rumah tangga yang menjaga halaman, kandang ternak, dan istal; kata iye berarti pemilik atau tuan. Ia mirip roh rumah Ev iyesi tetapi kurang baik hati, dan dianggap lebih berbahaya karena dapat mengancam ternak, terutama yang berbulu putih. Wujud perempuannya disebut Abzar Ana dan wujud lelakinya Abzar Ata.
long_description.en: In Turkic folklore Abzar iyesi is a household spirit guarding the courtyard, cattle shed and stable; iye means owner or master. It resembles the house spirit Ev iyesi but is less benevolent, and was thought more dangerous because it could threaten livestock, especially white-furred animals. Its female form is Abzar Ana and its male form Abzar Ata.

long_description.id: Pada malam hari ia kadang tampil sebagai manusia atau hewan. Ia menyayangi sebagian ternak dan menyiksa yang lain, sehingga orang harus menjaga hubungan baik dengannya dan sesekali memberinya persembahan.
long_description.en: At night it sometimes appears as a person or an animal. It cherishes some livestock and persecutes others, so people had to keep on good terms with it and occasionally make offerings.

short_description.id: Aitu adalah kata Polinesia untuk hantu atau roh yang sering jahat, tetapi di Tonga dan Samoa juga berarti dewa-dewa rendah dan pelindung keluarga dan desa.
short_description.en: Aitu is the Polynesian word for ghosts or spirits, often malevolent, but in Tonga and Samoa it also denotes lesser gods who are patrons and tutelary deities of families and villages.

long_description.id: Dalam bahasa-bahasa Polinesia, kata aitu merujuk pada hantu atau roh, sering kali jahat; kata ini umum di banyak bahasa Polinesia Barat dan Timur. Dalam bahasa Tahiti ia dapat berarti dewa atau roh, dalam bahasa Rarotonga, Samoa, dan Niue ia berarti hantu atau roh, dan dalam mitologi Māori ia merujuk pada penyakit, bencana, atau iblis.
long_description.en: Across Polynesian languages, aitu denotes ghosts or spirits that are frequently malevolent, and the word is shared by many languages of Western and Eastern Polynesia. In Tahitian it can mean god or spirit, in Rarotongan, Samoan and Niuean it means ghosts or spirits, and in Māori mythology it refers to sickness, calamity or demons.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Tonga, ʻaitu atau ʻeitu adalah dewa-dewa rendah, banyak di antaranya pelindung desa dan keluarga tertentu. Mereka sering berwujud tumbuhan atau hewan dan sering lebih kejam daripada dewa lain, serta dianggap berasal dari Samoa.
long_description.en: In the mythology of Tonga, ʻaitu or ʻeitu are minor gods, many serving as patrons of particular villages and families; they commonly appear as plants or animals, tend to be crueller than other gods, and are said to have come from Samoa.

long_description.id: Menurut salah satu sumber, saat lahir seorang Samoa dianggap berada di bawah asuhan suatu dewa, atau aitu. Dewa itu dianggap tampil dalam penjelmaan yang terlihat, misalnya belut, hiu, penyu, anjing, burung hantu, atau kadal, dan benda itu menjadi objek penghormatan. Orang bebas memakan penjelmaan dewa orang lain, tetapi memakan atau melukai penjelmaan dewanya sendiri dianggap membawa kematian; dewa dianggap membalas dengan menetap di tubuh orang itu.
long_description.en: According to one source, a Samoan was said at birth to come under the care of some god, or aitu. That god was thought to appear in a visible incarnation, such as the eel, shark, turtle, dog, owl or lizard, and the creature became an object of veneration. People ate freely of the incarnation of another man's god, but harming or eating that of one's own was thought to bring death; the god was believed to avenge the insult by taking up residence in the offender's body.

long_description.id: Golongan dewa pelindung rumah disebut aitu fale, atau dewa rumah, dan Aitu Langi adalah dewa-dewa langit yang dianggap jatuh dari langit atas panggilan seorang buta untuk melindungi putranya dari seorang kepala suku kanibal. Di Kepulauan Cook, Aitu juga nama suku-suku kuno yang datang dari timur, dan di budaya Austronesia lain kata ini sepadan dengan hantu atau antu dalam bahasa Indonesia dan Malaysia.
long_description.en: The class of tutelary deities is called aitu fale, "gods of the house", while Aitu Langi are sky gods said to have dropped from the heavens when a blind man called on them to protect his son from a cannibal chief. In the Cook Islands the name Aitu is also borne by ancient tribes that arrived from the east, and elsewhere in the Austronesian world the word has cognates such as hantu or antu in Malaysia and Indonesia.

claims.quote: A man would eat freely of what was regarded as the incarnation of the god of another man, but the incarnation of his own particular god he would consider it death to injure or to eat. The god was supposed to avenge the insult by taking up his abode in that person's body

statement.id: Seseorang bebas memakan penjelmaan dewa orang lain, tetapi menganggap kematian bila melukai atau memakan penjelmaan dewanya sendiri; dewa itu dianggap membalas penghinaan dengan menetap di tubuh orang tersebut.
statement.en: A man would eat freely of the incarnation of another man's god, but would consider it death to injure or eat the incarnation of his own god; the god was supposed to avenge the insult by taking up his abode in that person's body.

claims.quote: This class of genii, or tutelary deities, they called aitu fale, or gods of the house.

statement.id: Golongan jin atau dewa pelindung ini mereka sebut aitu fale, atau dewa rumah.
statement.en: This class of genii, or tutelary deities, they called aitu fale, or gods of the house.

claims.quote: Aitu Langi, or Gods of heaven. 1. These gods were supposed to have fallen from the heavens at the call of a blind man to protect his son from a cannibal chief.

statement.id: Aitu Langi, atau Dewa-dewa Langit: dewa-dewa ini dianggap jatuh dari langit atas panggilan seorang buta untuk melindungi putranya dari seorang kepala suku kanibal.
statement.en: Aitu Langi, or Gods of heaven: these gods were supposed to have fallen from the heavens at the call of a blind man to protect his son from a cannibal chief.

summary.id: Hantu atau roh yang sering jahat; di Tonga dewa-dewa yang sering lebih kejam daripada dewa lain.
summary.en: Ghosts or spirits, often malevolent; in Tonga gods often more cruel than other gods.

summary.id: Di Samoa, dewa pelindung rumah dan asuhan seseorang sejak lahir.
summary.en: In Samoa, tutelary gods of the house and of a person from birth.

short_description.id: Akashaguma adalah yōkai dari Shikoku yang menyerupai anak berambut merah dan tinggal di rumah warga; sebagian pendapat menggolongkannya dengan zashiki-warashi.
short_description.en: Akashaguma is a yōkai of Shikoku resembling a red-haired child that settles in people's houses; some theories group it with the zashiki-warashi.

long_description.id: Akashaguma adalah yōkai dari Shikoku yang menetap di rumah warga dan menyerupai anak berambut merah. Ada teori yang menggolongkannya sebagai sejenis zashiki-warashi. Ciri dan perilakunya berbeda dari daerah ke daerah.
long_description.en: Akashaguma is a yōkai of Shikoku that settles in people's houses and resembles a red-haired child. Some theories count it as a kind of zashiki-warashi. Its features and behavior differ from region to region.

long_description.id: Di Distrik Nii, ia diceritakan ribut di ruang zashiki dan memakan makanan di dapur setelah penghuni tertidur. Di Hiromi dan Uwajima ia disebut kobōzu, dan beberapa Akashaguma terlihat menghangatkan diri di perapian lalu lenyap ke bawah lantai. Di Tokushima dan Kagawa ia muncul dari bawah altar Buddha dan menggelitik kaki penghuni yang tidur; di Kagawa ia juga muncul di luar rumah dan konon terbang di pegunungan sambil berteriak.
long_description.en: In Nii district it is told to make noise in the zashiki room and eat food in the kitchen after residents fall asleep. In Hiromi and Uwajima it is called kobōzu, and several Akashaguma were seen warming themselves at a hearth and then vanishing under the floor. In Tokushima and Kagawa it appears from beneath the Buddhist altar and tickles the feet of sleeping residents; in Kagawa it also appears outdoors and is said to fly through the mountains shouting.

long_description.id: Dalam satu kisah, seorang nenek yang membeli rumah berhantu akhirnya pergi setelah terus digelitiki Akashaguma. Dalam kisah lain, sebuah keluarga kelelahan karena digelitiki, dan seorang pria pingsan setelah melihat Akashaguma berdiri di ladang. Sebuah anekdot dari Kagawa menyebut majikan yang memakai jenazah sebagai umpan untuk memancing dan menembak Akashaguma.
long_description.en: In one story, an old woman who bought a haunted house finally left after being repeatedly tickled by Akashaguma. In another, a household was exhausted by the tickling and a man fainted after seeing an Akashaguma standing in the field. An anecdote from Kagawa tells of an employer who used a corpse as bait to lure and shoot an Akashaguma.

long_description.id: Artikel zashiki-warashi menyebut Akashaguma sebagai makhluk yang mirip zashiki-warashi dan menjelaskan akashaguma sebagai bulu beruang yang dicelup merah. Orikuchi Shinobu memandangnya sebagai contoh kisah roh setia yang datang bekerja untuk sebuah rumah dan bila pergi rumah itu merosot.
long_description.en: The zashiki-warashi article lists Akashaguma among things similar to zashiki-warashi and explains akashaguma as red-dyed bear hair. Orikuchi Shinobu saw it as an example of a tale of a loyal spirit who comes to work for a house and whose departure brings the house to decline.

claims.quote: 赤シャグマ（あかシャグマ）は、四国に伝わる妖怪。人家に住み着く赤い髪の子供のような妖怪で、座敷童子の仲間とする説もある。

statement.id: Akashaguma adalah yōkai Shikoku menyerupai anak berambut merah.
statement.en: Akashaguma is a childlike red-haired yōkai of Shikoku.

claims.quote: 新居郡神戸村（現・西条市）などの町村の人家に住み着いていたとされる。夜に住人が寝静まった後で座敷で騒ぎ始め、台所にある食べ物を食べてしまう。

statement.id: Mereka konon menetap di rumah-rumah warga di desa seperti Desa Kōbe, Distrik Nii (kini Saijō); setelah penghuni tertidur pada malam hari, mereka mulai ribut di ruang zashiki dan memakan makanan di dapur.
statement.en: They are said to have lived in houses in towns and villages such as Kōbe village, Nii district (now Saijō); after the residents fall asleep at night they start making noise in the zashiki room and eat the food in the kitchen.

claims.quote: 広見町（現・鬼北町）や宇和島市の伝承では小坊主（こぼうず）とも呼ばれており、山仕事に出かけた男が家に帰ってくると、薄暗い家の中、囲炉裏で数人の赤シャグマが暖をとっており、男の帰宅に気づいた赤シャグマたちは床下へと姿を消したという。

statement.id: Dalam tradisi Kota Hiromi (kini Kihoku) dan Uwajima, mereka juga disebut kobōzu; seorang pria yang pulang dari kerja gunung mendapati beberapa Akashaguma menghangatkan diri di perapian rumah yang remang, dan mereka lenyap ke bawah lantai begitu menyadari kepulangannya.
statement.en: In traditions of Hiromi town (now Kihoku) and Uwajima they are also called kobōzu; a man returning from mountain work found several Akashaguma warming themselves at the hearth in the dim house, and they vanished under the floor when they noticed him.

claims.quote: かつて「化け物が出ると」と噂される古い一軒家があり、誰も住もうとしない中、ある老婆がその家を買って自宅とした。しかし夜になると噂通り赤シャグマが現れ、老婆をくすぐって悪戯した。老婆は結局、その家を立ち退いたという。

statement.id: Sebuah kisah menceritakan seorang nenek yang membeli rumah tua yang digosipkan berhantu; Akashaguma muncul pada malam hari seperti kabar dan menggelitikinya sebagai keisengan, dan akhirnya sang nenek meninggalkan rumah itu.
statement.en: A story tells of an old woman who bought a house rumored to be haunted by a monster; Akashaguma appeared at night as rumored and tickled her as a prank, and she eventually left the house.

claims.quote: 徳島県（阿波国）での例 ... 夜になると仏壇の下から現れ、眠っている住人の足をくすぐるなどの悪戯を働く。

statement.id: Dalam tradisi Tokushima (Awa), Akashaguma muncul dari bawah altar Buddha pada malam hari dan berbuat iseng seperti menggelitik kaki penghuni yang tidur.
statement.en: In the Tokushima (Awa) tradition, Akashaguma appear from beneath the Buddhist altar at night and play pranks such as tickling the feet of sleeping residents.

claims.quote: 徳島の例と同様に香川でも、赤シャグマは夜中に人の足をくすぐるといわれる。また香川の赤シャグマ独自の特徴としては、家の中のみならず野外でも赤シャグマが現れるとする説があり、山中で大声を張り上げながら空を飛ぶともいう。

statement.id: Seperti di Tokushima, di Kagawa Akashaguma juga dikatakan menggelitik kaki orang pada tengah malam; ciri khas Kagawa adalah teori bahwa mereka muncul juga di luar rumah dan konon terbang di udara di pegunungan sambil berteriak keras.
statement.en: As in Tokushima, in Kagawa Akashaguma are also said to tickle people's feet at midnight; a Kagawa-specific feature is the idea that they appear outdoors as well as indoors, and they are said to fly through the sky in the mountains shouting loudly.

claims.quote: 三好郡足代村のある家で、住人たちが夜寝た後、赤シャグマが現れて彼らをくすぐり、住人たちはすっかり疲れてしまった。翌日、その家の1人の男が畑仕事に出たところ、そこに赤シャグマが立っていた。それを見た男は、家へ駆け込むなり気絶してしまったという。

statement.id: Di sebuah rumah di Desa Ashiro, Distrik Miyoshi, Akashaguma muncul setelah penghuni tidur dan menggelitik mereka hingga kelelahan; keesokan harinya seorang pria melihat Akashaguma berdiri di ladang dan pingsan begitu berlari masuk rumah.
statement.en: In a house in Ashiro village, Miyoshi district, Akashaguma appeared after the residents slept and tickled them until they were exhausted; the next day a man working in the field saw an Akashaguma standing there and fainted as soon as he ran into the house.

claims.quote: 雇い主は墓をあばき、その屍を若者に運ばせて山へ行き、屍を餌にして赤シャグマをおびき寄せ、射止めたという。

statement.id: Dalam sebuah anekdot, seorang majikan membongkar makam, menyuruh seorang pemuda membawa jenazahnya ke gunung, memakainya sebagai umpan untuk memancing Akashaguma, lalu menembaknya.
statement.en: In one anecdote, an employer digs up a grave, has a youth carry the corpse into the mountains, uses it as bait to lure an Akashaguma, and shoots it.

claims.quote: 座敷童子に類するものに、遠州門谷村（現・愛知県新城市門谷）の「座敷坊主」、徳島の「アカシャグマ」がある。四国金毘羅宮の、奥の院周辺の家には、夜になると仏壇の中から「アカシャグマ」が出てきたという。

statement.id: Artikel Zashiki-warashi menyebut Akashaguma dari Tokushima sebagai makhluk yang mirip zashiki-warashi; di rumah-rumah sekitar Okunoin Kompira-gū di Shikoku, Akashaguma konon keluar dari dalam altar Buddha pada malam hari.
statement.en: The zashiki-warashi article lists the Akashaguma of Tokushima among things similar to zashiki-warashi; in houses around the Okunoin of Shikoku's Kompira-gū, Akashaguma are said to have come out of the Buddhist altar at night.

claims.quote: アカシャグマとは、赤く染めたクマの毛のことで、これを被った小さな子供のようなものが、家の持ち主の老婆を毎晩くすぐったという。

statement.id: Artikel itu menyebut akashaguma sebagai bulu beruang yang dicelup merah; sesuatu seperti anak kecil yang memakainya konon menggelitik nenek pemilik rumah setiap malam.
statement.en: The article says that akashaguma means red-dyed bear hair, and that something like a small child wearing it is said to have tickled the old woman owner of the house every night.

claims.quote: 民俗学者・折口信夫はオクナイサマ、座敷坊主、アカシャグマ、沖縄のキジムナー、壱岐のガアタロなどの例を引いて、外の土地のある家のために働きに来る忠実な精霊がいて、いなくなると家が衰えると言う型の話と見た。

statement.id: Folklorwan Orikuchi Shinobu mengutip Akashaguma bersama Okunaisama, Zashiki-bōzu, Kijimuna Okinawa, dan Gaataro Iki sebagai contoh kisah roh setia yang datang bekerja untuk sebuah rumah dan bila pergi rumah itu merosot.
statement.en: The folklorist Orikuchi Shinobu cited Akashaguma along with Okunaisama, Zashiki-bōzu, Okinawa's Kijimuna and Iki's Gaataro as examples of a tale type in which a loyal spirit comes to work for a house and the house declines when it leaves.

short_description.id: Negro-d'Água adalah makhluk sungai setengah amfibi yang membalikkan kano nelayan yang menolak memberinya ikan [akva-nigrulo-c01, akva-nigrulo-c02].
short_description.en: The Negro-d'Água is a half-amphibian river being that capsizes the canoes of fishermen who refuse it a fish [akva-nigrulo-c01, akva-nigrulo-c02].

long_description.id: Negro-d'Água menghuni banyak sungai seperti Rio Tocantins dan Rio São Francisco [akva-nigrulo-c01]. Ia muncul dengan tawa keras, bertangan dan berkaki seperti bebek, dan membalikkan kano nelayan yang menolak memberinya ikan [akva-nigrulo-c02]. Wujudnya perpaduan manusia dan amfibi, bersirip dan bersisik [akva-nigrulo-c04].
long_description.en: The Negro-d'Água inhabits many rivers such as the Tocantins and São Francisco [akva-nigrulo-c01]. It appears laughing loudly, with duck-like hands and feet, capsizing the canoes of fishermen who refuse it a fish [akva-nigrulo-c02]. It is a fusion of man and amphibian, with fins and scales [akva-nigrulo-c04].

long_description.id: Sebagian nelayan melempar sebotol cachaça ke sungai agar perahunya aman [akva-nigrulo-c03]. Câmara Cascudo menganggapnya turunan Ipupiara [akva-nigrulo-c05].
long_description.en: Some fishermen throw a bottle of cachaça into the river to keep their boats safe [akva-nigrulo-c03]. Câmara Cascudo considers it derived from the Ipupiara [akva-nigrulo-c05].

long_description.id: Dalam kamus folklornya, Cascudo menyebut Negro-d'água di antara nama lain Caboclo-d'água dan mengutip José A. Teixeira [akva-nigrulo-c06]. Menurut kutipan itu, ia mendiami tepi sungai-sungai di lembah Paraná, serba hitam, berkepala botak, bertangan dan berkaki bebek [akva-nigrulo-c07]. Ia muncul di antara bebatuan pada senja atau malam berbulan purnama dan berusaha membalikkan kano [akva-nigrulo-c08]; menembaknya sia-sia karena peluru memantul dari kulitnya yang berbulu [akva-nigrulo-c09]. Cascudo juga menulis bahwa Ipupiara akan menurunkan Caboclo do Rio atau Negro do Rio yang membalikkan perahu [akva-nigrulo-c10].
long_description.en: In his folklore dictionary, Cascudo lists Negro-d'água among the other names of the Caboclo-d'água and quotes José A. Teixeira [akva-nigrulo-c06]. According to that passage it inhabits the banks of rivers in the Paraná valley, is all black and bald-headed, with duck hands and feet [akva-nigrulo-c07]. It appears among rocks at dusk or on moonlit nights and tries to overturn canoes [akva-nigrulo-c08]; shooting at it is foolish because bullets strike its hairy hide [akva-nigrulo-c09]. Cascudo also writes that the Ipupiara gives rise to the Caboclo do Rio or Negro do Rio, which overturns boats [akva-nigrulo-c10].

cultural_context.id: Nelayan melempar sebotol cachaça ke sungai agar perahunya tidak dibalikkan [akva-nigrulo-c03].
cultural_context.en: Fishermen throw cachaça into the river so their boats are not overturned [akva-nigrulo-c03].

note.id: Cascudo menganggapnya turunan Ipupiara; ia menulis bahwa Ipupiara akan menurunkan Caboclo do Rio atau Negro do Rio.
note.en: Cascudo considers it derived from the Ipupiara; he writes that the Ipupiara gives rise to the Caboclo do Rio or Negro do Rio.

claims.quote: Diz a lenda que o Negro-d'Água ou Nego-d'Água habita diversos rios, tais como o Rio Tocantins, o Rio Grande, Rio Grande, oeste da Bahia e Rio São Francisco

statement.id: Menurut legenda, Negro-d'Água atau Nego-d'Água menghuni banyak sungai, seperti Rio Tocantins, Rio Grande, dan Rio São Francisco.
statement.en: Legend says the Negro-d'Água or Nego-d'Água inhabits many rivers, such as the Tocantins, Rio Grande and São Francisco.

claims.quote: Manifestando-se com suas gargalhadas, negro, careca e com mãos e pés de pato, ele derruba a canoa dos pescadores, se eles se recusarem a lhe dar um peixe.

statement.id: Ia muncul dengan tawa terbahak-bahak, berkepala botak, bertangan dan berkaki seperti bebek, dan membalikkan kano nelayan yang menolak memberinya ikan.
statement.en: It appears laughing loudly, bald, with duck-like hands and feet, and capsizes the canoes of fishermen who refuse it a fish.

claims.quote: levam uma garrafa de cachaça e a atiram para dentro do rio, para que não tenham sua embarcação virada.

statement.id: Sebagian nelayan melempar sebotol cachaça ke sungai agar perahunya tidak dibalikkan.
statement.en: Some fishermen throw a bottle of cachaça into the river so their boat is not overturned.

claims.quote: ele seria a fusão de homem negro alto e forte com um anfíbio. Apresenta nadadeiras e corpo coberto de escamas mistas com a pele.

statement.id: Wujudnya perpaduan lelaki tinggi kuat dengan amfibi, bersirip, dan bertubuh bersisik bercampur kulit.
statement.en: It is a fusion of a tall, strong man and an amphibian, with fins and scales mixed with skin.

claims.quote: Câmara Cascudo chama-o "Negro do Rio" e o considera um derivado do Ipupiara.

statement.id: Câmara Cascudo menyebutnya "Negro do Rio" dan menganggapnya turunan Ipupiara.
statement.en: Câmara Cascudo calls it "Negro do Rio" and considers it derived from the Ipupiara.

claims.quote: Moleque-d'água, Caboclo, Negro- “d'água, Sobre o Negro-d'água escre- ve José A. Teixeira (Folclore Goiano,

statement.id: Dalam verbete Caboclo-d'Água, Cascudo mencatat Negro-d'água di antara nama lain makhluk itu dan mengutip uraian José A. Teixeira (Folclore Goiano) tentangnya.
statement.en: In his Caboclo-d'Água entry, Cascudo lists Negro-d'água among that being's other names and quotes José A. Teixeira (Folclore Goiano) about it.

claims.quote: Habita as mar- gens dos rios que correm pelo vão do Paraná. É todo preto. Cabeça pelada. Mãos e pés de pato.

statement.id: Dalam kutipan Teixeira yang dimuat Cascudo, Negro-d'água mendiami tepi sungai-sungai yang mengalir di lembah Paraná; ia serba hitam, berkepala botak, bertangan dan berkaki bebek.
statement.en: In the passage by Teixeira quoted by Cascudo, the Negro-d'água inhabits the banks of rivers running through the Paraná valley; it is all black, bald-headed, with duck hands and feet.

claims.quote: Aparece entre pedras, à tardinha ou em noites de luar, a canoeiros e pescadores do ... e seus afluentes. E procura virar a canoa.

statement.id: Menurut kutipan itu, ia muncul di antara bebatuan (pedras) pada senja (à tardinha) atau malam berbulan purnama (noites de luar) kepada pendayung kano dan nelayan, dan berusaha membalikkan kano (virar a canoa).
statement.en: According to the passage, it appears among rocks (pedras) at dusk (à tardinha) or on moonlit nights (noites de luar) to canoeists and fishermen, and tries to overturn the canoe (virar a canoa).

claims.quote: É bobagem atirar bala: bate no couro peludo do negro

statement.id: Menurut kutipan itu, menembaknya sia-sia karena peluru memantul dari kulit berbulu si hitam.
statement.en: According to the passage, shooting at it is foolish: the bullet strikes the hairy hide of the black one.

claims.quote: O Ipupiara dará o Caboclo do Rio ou o Negro do Rio, virando embarcações, afogando,

statement.id: Cascudo menulis bahwa Ipupiara akan menurunkan Caboclo do Rio atau Negro do Rio, yang membalikkan perahu dan menenggelamkan orang.
statement.en: Cascudo writes that the Ipupiara gives rise to the Caboclo do Rio or Negro do Rio, which overturns boats and drowns people.

long_description.id: Alambala adalah raja raksasa dalam mitologi India, putra Jatasura. Ia bertempur di pihak Kaurava dalam perang Kurukshetra.
long_description.en: Alambala is a rakshasa king in Indian mythology, the son of Jatasura. He fights for the Kauravas in the Kurukshetra War.

long_description.id: Ia bergabung dengan Duryodhana untuk membalas pembunuhan ayahnya oleh Bhima. Duryodhana menugaskannya melawan Ghatotkacha. Ghatotkacha akhirnya membunuhnya dengan mengangkat dan menghantamkan tubuhnya ke tanah.

short_description.id: Alraune adalah akar mandragora berwujud manusia dalam kepercayaan Jerman, yang dianggap memegang nasib manusia dan, bila dirawat dengan baik, meramalkan masa depan.
short_description.en: The alraune is a human-shaped mandrake root in German belief, thought to hold people's fate in its power and, if well cared for, to foretell the future.

long_description.id: Alraune (kata Jerman untuk mandragora) adalah makhluk legenda yang konon dimiliki bangsa Jermanik kuno: akar mandragora yang menggenggam nasib manusia. Menurut legenda, pemiliknya harus memberinya pakaian rapi, membaringkannya dalam peti kecil, memandikannya setiap pekan dengan anggur dan air, serta memberinya makan dan minum setiap kali bersantap; bila tidak, alih-alih meramalkan masa depan, ia menjerit seperti bayi kelaparan.
long_description.en: Alraune (German for mandrake) is a legendary being said to have been kept by the ancient Germanic peoples: a mandrake root holding human fate. Legend says its owner had to dress it neatly, lay it in a small box, bathe it weekly in wine and water and feed it at every meal; otherwise, instead of foretelling the future, it would scream like a starving infant.

long_description.id: Kisah ini berakar pada Abad Pertengahan Jerman. Para alkemis percaya akar mandragora yang samar-samar berwujud manusia tumbuh dari sperma orang yang digantung, sehingga akar itu sering dicari di bawah tiang gantungan. Hanya akar berwujud tubuh manusia yang dianggap bertuah; akar ini dipakai dalam ramuan cinta, dan buahnya diyakini membantu kehamilan.
long_description.en: The tale goes back to the German Middle Ages. Alchemists believed the vaguely human-shaped mandrake root grew from the semen of hanged men, so it was often sought beneath the gallows. Only roots shaped like a human body were thought to have power; the root went into love potions, and its fruit was believed to aid conception.

long_description.id: Mencabutnya memerlukan persiapan: tanah di sekitarnya digali, tiga lingkaran sihir digambar dengan pedang, lalu seekor anjing hitam yang diikat pada tanaman itu menariknya keluar. Akar yang tercabut diyakini menjerit dengan suara manusia yang membunuh siapa pun yang mendengarnya, sehingga anjing itulah yang mati. Akar itu juga dikatakan mengangguk bila jawaban atas suatu pertanyaan adalah "ya".
long_description.en: Pulling one up took preparation: the soil around it was dug away, three magic circles were drawn with a sword, and a black dog tied to the plant dragged it out. The uprooted root was believed to scream with a human voice that killed whoever heard it, so the dog was the one to die. The root was also said to nod when the answer to a question was 'yes'.

short_description.id: Amanozako adalah dewi garang dalam mitologi Jepang yang lahir dari kegarangan Susanoo, digambarkan berkepala mirip binatang, dan dianggap leluhur tengu serta amanojaku.
short_description.en: Amanozako is a fierce goddess in Japanese mythology born from Susanoo's ferocious spirit, described with a beast-like head and popularly regarded as ancestor of the tengu and amanojaku.

long_description.id: Amanozako (天逆毎, "langit menentang segala hal") adalah dewi garang yang disebut dalam Kujiki. Menurut Kujiki, ia muncul ketika Susanoo membiarkan roh garangnya (ara-mitama) menumpuk di dalam dirinya hingga memuntahkannya keluar. Wakan Sansai Zue memberi gambaran serupa: ia lahir dari kegarangan Susanoo yang terembus keluar.
long_description.en: Amanozako (天逆毎, "heaven opposing everything") is a monstrous goddess mentioned in the Kujiki. The Kujiki is said to relate that she arose after Susanoo allowed his own fierce spirit (ara-mitama) to accumulate within him until he spat her out. The Wakan Sansai Zue gives a similar picture: she was born from Susanoo's ferocity breathed out.

long_description.id: Wakan Sansai Zue menggambarkannya berwatak murka, berkepala binatang dengan hidung panjang, telinga panjang, dan taring kuat yang dapat mengunyah bilah logam hingga rusak. Ia dikatakan melawan kelaziman dan melakukan kebalikan dari yang diharapkan masyarakat, dan mengamuk hebat bila keinginannya tidak terpenuhi.
long_description.en: The Wakan Sansai Zue describes her as furious-tempered, with a beastly head, long nose, long ears and fangs strong enough to chew metal blades ragged. She is said to go against conformity and do the opposite of what society expects, and to fly into a terrible rage when she does not get what she wants.

long_description.id: Ia melahirkan sendiri seorang anak, Amanosaku, yang kemudian menjadi raja sembilan langit dan menguasai dewa-dewa liar dan pembangkang. Amanozako dianggap leluhur tengu dan amanojaku, dan 諦忍 menyebutnya "leluhur tengu Jepang", walau pandangan itu tidak tampak di buku lain. Toriyama Sekien menggambarnya dalam Konjaku Gazu Zoku Hyakki.
long_description.en: She bore a child on her own, Amanosaku, who later became king of the nine heavens and ruled the wild and rebellious gods. Amanozako is regarded as the ancestor of the tengu and amanojaku, and 諦忍 called her an "ancestor of the Japanese tengu", though this view appears in no other book. Toriyama Sekien illustrated her in the Konjaku Gazu Zoku Hyakki.

short_description.id: Anchanchu adalah vampir pengubah wujud dari wilayah Aymara di Bolivia.
short_description.en: The anchanchu is a shapeshifting vampire of the Aymara region of Bolivia.

long_description.id: Anchanchu adalah vampir legendaris Andes yang terutama berasal dari wilayah Aymara di Bolivia. Ia dikatakan berubah wujud menjadi pelancong tua yang tak berdaya, perempuan Aymara kaya bergigi emas, perempuan asing yang memikat, atau hewan mengerikan. Saat orang yang lewat menawarkan bantuan, ia mengisap darahnya hingga korban meninggal; ia disebut makhluk jahat yang paling ditakuti bangsa Aymara karena sifatnya yang mematikan.
long_description.en: The anchanchu is a legendary Andean vampire that largely comes from the Aymara region of Bolivia. It is said to change shape into a helpless old traveler, a rich gold-toothed Aymara woman, a seductive foreign woman, or a monstrous animal. When a passerby offers help it drinks the victim's blood until they die; it is described as the evil being the Aymara fear most because of its lethality.

long_description.id: Catatan lama dari Bolivia memberi gambaran lain. M. Rigoberto Paredes, dalam bukunya tentang mitos Bolivia, menulis bahwa Anchanchu dilukiskan sebagai lelaki tua kerdil yang berperut buncit, botak, dan berkepala besar. Menurut Paredes, ia dikatakan tinggal di gua, dasar sungai, dan bangunan yang runtuh dan terbengkalai, memikat korban dengan sikap manis, serta menimbulkan angin kencang dan pusaran angin ketika berjalan di jalan.
long_description.en: An older account from Bolivia gives another picture. M. Rigoberto Paredes, in his book on Bolivian myths, wrote that the Anchanchu is portrayed as a little old dwarf, pot-bellied, bald and big-headed. According to Paredes, it is said to live in caves, at the bottom of rivers and in ruined, abandoned buildings, to lure victims with sweet manners, and to raise strong winds and whirlwinds when it travels the roads.

long_description.id: Paredes menyebutnya dewa yang sinister, yang selalu tersenyum sambil menyiapkan kerusakan terbesar. Orang jarang berani bermalam di dekat sungai atau rumah kosong karena takut kepadanya, dan nama makhluk itu pun enggan diucapkan. Sebuah glosarium dari Universitas Katolik Bolivia menyebut Anchanchu sebagai kekuatan yang relatif negatif yang tinggal di dasar sungai, gua, celah gunung, jurang, dan rumah kosong.
long_description.en: Paredes calls it a sinister deity that smiles all the while it prepares the greatest harm. People rarely dare to spend the night near rivers or in empty houses for fear of it, and they avoid even pronouncing its name. A glossary from the Bolivian Catholic University calls Anchanchu a relatively negative force that dwells in river bottoms, caves, mountain crevices, ravines and uninhabited houses.

long_description.id: Menurut tradisi yang dicatat, korban anchanchu harus segera ditangani dengan bantuan yatiri atau amauta, yang membuat persembahan bernama ch'iyara misa ("meja hitam"). Anchanchu juga disebut saudara tidak sah Ekeko (Iqiqu). Di Peru ia dikenal sebagai duende mirip kurcaci bernama Muki.
long_description.en: Tradition holds that people attacked by an anchanchu need quick treatment from yatiris or amautas, who prepare an offering called ch'iyara misa ("black table"). The anchanchu is also called the illegitimate brother of Ekeko (Iqiqu). In Peru it is known as a dwarf-like duende called Muki.

description.en: A dwarf-like duende living underground, fond of gold.

statement.en: The anchanchu is a legendary Andean vampire mainly from the Aymara region of Bolivia.

claims.quote: It shapeshifts into the form of a helpless, elderly traveler, a rich Aymara woman with gold teeth, a seductive gringa, or a monstrous animal.

statement.id: Ia menyamar sebagai pelancong tua tak berdaya, perempuan Aymara kaya bergigi emas, perempuan asing yang memikat, atau hewan mengerikan.
statement.en: It takes the form of a helpless old traveler, a rich gold-toothed Aymara woman, a seductive gringa or a monstrous animal.

claims.quote: When a passerby offers to help, the anchanchu victimizes them and drinks their blood, causing them to die of blood loss or disease.

statement.id: Saat orang lewat menawarkan bantuan, anchanchu mengisap darahnya hingga ia mati.
statement.en: When a passerby offers help, it drinks their blood until they die.

claims.quote: In Peru, the anchanchu is a duende, similar to a dwarf. Called Muki or Muqui, it lives underground and has a penchant for gold.

statement.id: Di Peru, anchanchu adalah duende mirip kurcaci bernama Muki yang tinggal di bawah tanah dan menyukai emas.
statement.en: In Peru the anchanchu is a dwarf-like duende called Muki, living underground and fond of gold.

claims.quote: The anchanchu is the most feared evil being among the Aymara people due to its lethality.

statement.id: Anchanchu adalah makhluk jahat yang paling ditakuti di kalangan bangsa Aymara karena sifatnya yang mematikan.
statement.en: The anchanchu is the most feared evil being among the Aymara people because of its lethality.

claims.quote: Anchanchus take advantage of peoples' compassion to suck blood from their lips or heart.

statement.id: Anchanchu memanfaatkan belas kasihan orang untuk mengisap darah dari bibir atau jantung mereka.
statement.en: Anchanchus take advantage of people's compassion to suck blood from their lips or heart.

claims.quote: According to tradition, anchanchu victims must be treated quickly with the help of yatiris or amautas, who make an offering known as ch'iyara misa ("black table")

statement.id: Menurut tradisi, korban anchanchu harus segera ditangani dengan bantuan yatiri atau amauta, yang membuat persembahan bernama ch'iyara misa ("meja hitam").
statement.en: According to tradition, anchanchu victims must be treated quickly with the help of yatiris or amautas, who make an offering known as ch'iyara misa ("black table").

claims.quote: According to tradition, the anchanchu is the illegitimate brother of Ekeko (Iqiqu)

statement.id: Menurut tradisi, anchanchu adalah saudara tidak sah dari Ekeko (Iqiqu).
statement.en: According to tradition, the anchanchu is the illegitimate brother of Ekeko (Iqiqu).

claims.quote: While many popular online sources depict anchanchu as a demonic figure, Aymara mythology casts him as a gatekeeper of the underground mineral world, and homage must be paid to anchanchu before mining the Earth's resources.

statement.id: Meskipun banyak sumber populer di internet menggambarkan anchanchu sebagai sosok iblis, mitologi Aymara menempatkannya sebagai penjaga gerbang dunia mineral bawah tanah, dan penghormatan harus diberikan kepadanya sebelum menambang sumber daya Bumi.
statement.en: While many popular online sources depict anchanchu as a demonic figure, Aymara mythology casts him as a gatekeeper of the underground mineral world, and homage must be paid to him before mining the Earth's resources.

claims.quote: The anchanchu lives in the most desolate caves and grottoes of the altiplano, a plateau in the Andes Mountains.

statement.id: Anchanchu tinggal di gua dan relung paling sunyi di altiplano, dataran tinggi di Pegunungan Andes.
statement.en: The anchanchu lives in the most desolate caves and grottoes of the altiplano, a plateau in the Andes Mountains.

claims.quote: viejecito enano, barrigón, calvo, de cabeza grande y

statement.id: Paredes menulis bahwa Anchanchu digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua kerdil yang berperut buncit, botak, dan berkepala besar.
statement.en: Paredes writes that the Anchanchu is portrayed as a little old dwarf, pot-bellied, bald, and big-headed.

claims.quote: que mora en las cuevas, en el fondo de los ríos y en edificios ruinosos y abandonados

statement.id: Menurut Paredes, ia dikatakan tinggal di gua, di dasar sungai, dan di bangunan yang runtuh dan terbengkalai.
statement.en: According to Paredes, it is said to dwell in caves, at the bottom of rivers, and in ruined and abandoned buildings.

claims.quote: El Anchanchu atrae a sus víctimas con sus salamerías, y las recibe regocijado y

statement.id: Paredes menulis bahwa Anchanchu memikat korbannya dengan sikap manis yang berlebihan dan menyambut mereka dengan gembira.
statement.en: Paredes writes that the Anchanchu draws in his victims with his flattering courtesies and welcomes them gladly.

claims.quote: El Anchanchu es una deidad siniestra, que sonríe siempre y sonriendo prepara y causa los mayores daños

statement.id: Paredes menyebut Anchanchu sebagai dewa yang sinister, yang selalu tersenyum dan sambil tersenyum menyiapkan serta menimbulkan kerusakan terbesar.
statement.en: Paredes calls the Anchanchu a sinister deity who always smiles and, smiling, prepares and causes the greatest harm.

claims.quote: Cuando transita por los caminos, produce huracanes y remolinos de viento

statement.id: Menurut Paredes, ketika berjalan di jalan ia menimbulkan angin kencang dan pusaran angin.
statement.en: According to Paredes, when it travels along the roads it produces hurricanes and whirlwinds.

claims.quote: rara vez se atreve a pernoctar cerca a los ríos o en casas deshabitadas ... terrible deidad, cuyo nombre excusa aún pronunciarlo

statement.id: Paredes mencatat bahwa orang Aymara jarang berani bermalam di dekat sungai atau di rumah kosong, karena takut pada dewa yang mengerikan ini, yang namanya pun enggan diucapkan.
statement.en: Paredes records that people rarely dare to spend the night (pernoctar) near rivers or in uninhabited houses (casas deshabitadas), out of fear of this terrible deity whose name they avoid even pronouncing.

claims.quote: Una fuerza relativamente negativa que mora en los fondos de los ríos, en las cuevas y grietas de las montañas, en las quebradas, bajo tierra en lugares desolados y en casas deshabitadas.

statement.id: Glosarium Universitas Katolik Bolivia menyebut Anchanchu sebagai kekuatan yang relatif negatif yang tinggal di dasar sungai, gua dan celah gunung, jurang, bawah tanah di tempat sunyi, dan rumah kosong.
statement.en: The Bolivian Catholic University glossary calls Anchanchu a relatively negative force that dwells in river bottoms, in mountain caves and crevices, in ravines, underground in desolate places, and in uninhabited houses.

topic.en: Nature and form of the anchanchu

summary.id: Satu sumber menggambarkannya sebagai vampir pengubah wujud yang membunuh penolongnya.
summary.en: One source describes it as a shapeshifting vampire that kills those who help it.

summary.id: Paredes melukiskannya sebagai lelaki tua kerdil yang memikat korban dengan sikap manis.
summary.en: Paredes portrays it as a little old dwarf who lures victims with sweet manners.

summary.id: Menurut sumber pertama itu, mitologi Aymara menempatkan anchanchu sebagai penjaga gerbang dunia mineral bawah tanah yang harus dihormati sebelum penambangan, berbeda dengan gambaran iblis di banyak sumber populer.
summary.en: According to that first source, Aymara mythology casts the anchanchu as a gatekeeper of the underground mineral world to be honored before mining, unlike the demonic picture in many popular sources.

gaps.searched: Tidak ada gambar Commons yang terbukti menggambarkan makhluk ini; artikel Wikipedia-nya tidak memuat ilustrasi.

Dicari di arsip.org (teks penuh), Google, dan situs jurnal. Dipakai: Paredes (1920, Internet Archive, salinan Universitas Toronto) dan glosarium UCB (SciELO Bolivia). Tidak dipakai: mythlok.com, moonmausoleum.com, pantheon.org (tanpa penulis atau tidak bisa diperiksa); Fernandez 1998 (Iqiqu y anchanchu) dan Estermann (Filosofia andina) tidak punya teks terbuka. Kamus Funk & Wagnalls hanya tersedia sebagai pinjaman terbatas.

short_description.id: Aobōzu adalah yōkai Jepang yang muncul dalam beragam legenda.
short_description.en: Aobōzu is a Japanese yōkai found in a range of legends.

long_description.id: Aobōzu adalah yōkai Jepang yang muncul dalam beragam legenda. Rincian cerita mengenai makhluk ini berbeda-beda. Toriyama Sekien memasukkannya ke dalam karya ilustrasi yōkai.
long_description.en: Aobōzu is a Japanese yōkai found in a range of legends. Details of the tales differ. Toriyama Sekien included it in an illustrated yōkai collection.

long_description.id: Makhluk ini sering digambarkan sebagai sosok besar menyerupai pendeta. Di Gifu dan Hiroshima, beberapa kisah menghubungkannya dengan tanuki yang menyamar. Di Shizuoka, ada kisah aobōzu menculik anak yang melintasi ladang gandum menjelang senja.
long_description.en: It is often portrayed as a large priest-like figure. Some Gifu and Hiroshima tales describe a disguised tanuki. A Shizuoka tale says it takes children crossing wheat fields near dusk.

long_description.id: Menurut sumber lain, aobōzu umumnya digambarkan sebagai pendeta besar bermata satu berkulit biru yang lekat dengan sihir, tetapi cerita setempat berbeda dalam ukuran, jumlah mata, dan tempat tinggal. Di Okayama, mereka raksasa bermata dua yang menghuni rumah kosong. Dalam kisah lain mereka muncul di ladang gandum atau di jalan gelap yang sepi.
long_description.en: According to another source, aobōzu are generally depicted as large, one-eyed, blue-skinned priests closely tied to magic, but local tales differ in size, number of eyes and dwelling. In Okayama they are two-eyed giants living in empty houses. Elsewhere they turn up in wheat fields or along gloomy, deserted roads.

long_description.id: Di Kagawa, aobōzu muncul larut malam di hadapan perempuan muda dan menanyakan apakah mereka mau tergantung di leher. Di Yamaguchi, mereka dianggap dewa kecil sebesar anak-anak yang menantang orang bergulat sumo di jalan. Toriyama Sekien disebut sebagai yang pertama mencatatnya, dengan ilustrasi tanpa keterangan selain nama; kata ao dapat berarti biru atau hijau dan menandakan sifat belum dewasa.
long_description.en: In Kagawa, aobōzu appear late at night to young women and ask whether they would like to hang by the neck. In Yamaguchi they are regarded as minor deities, only as big as children, who challenge people to sumo on the road. Toriyama Sekien is said to have been the first to record it, with an illustration carrying no description beyond the name; the word ao can mean blue or green and denote immaturity.

statement.en: Some Gifu and Hiroshima tales describe a disguised tanuki.

statement.en: A Shizuoka tale says it takes children crossing wheat fields near dusk.

claims.quote: In Okayama, they are described as two-eyed giants who take up residence in abandoned or uninhabited homes. In other stories, they appear in wheat fields, or on dark, lonely roads.

statement.en: In Okayama they are described as two-eyed giants who occupy abandoned or uninhabited houses; in other stories they appear in wheat fields or on dark, lonely roads.

claims.quote: In Kagawa, ao bōzu appear late at night to young women and ask them, “Would you like to hang by your neck?”

claims.quote: In Yamaguchi, they are considered minor deities. They appear before humans on the road and challenge them to sumo matches. Because Yamaguchi’s ao bōzu are only as big as children, many a person has foolishly accepted the challenge

statement.en: Toriyama Sekien is said to have been the first to record the ao bōzu, and his illustration carried no description other than its name.

claims.quote: From its name, we can glean a little bit of information; the word ao means blue or green, and can denote immaturity and inexperience.

short_description.id: Apshait adalah monster Mesir yang digambarkan sebagai kumbang besar pemakan jasad dan disebut dalam bab 36 Kitab Orang Mati, bab yang berfungsi menahannya.
short_description.en: The Apshait is an Egyptian monster pictured as a big beetle that devours corpses, named in chapter 36 of the Book of the Dead, the chapter meant to keep it back.

long_description.id: Apshait adalah monster Mesir yang digambarkan sebagai kumbang besar pemakan daging yang melahap jasad. Namanya muncul dalam Kitab Orang Mati bab 36. Dalam terjemahan Renouf, bab XXXVI berjudul "Bab yang menahan Āpshait".
long_description.en: The Apshait is an Egyptian monster pictured as a big flesh-eating beetle that devours corpses. Its name appears in the Book of the Dead, chapter 36. In Renouf's translation, chapter XXXVI is titled "Chapter whereby the Āpshait is kept back".

long_description.id: Teks bab itu berupa ucapan pengusir: pembicara menyuruh sosok berbibir terbuka itu pergi, menyebut dirinya Chnemu, Tuan Shennu, dan mengaku membawa kata-kata para dewa kepada Rā. Catatan Renouf menyebut kata terakhir bab itu meragukan, dan salah satu papirus memuat Nebes, dewi berkepala singa.
long_description.en: The chapter text is a repelling formula in which the speaker tells the open-lipped figure to go away, names himself Chnemu, Lord of Shennu, and claims to bring the words of the gods to Rā. Renouf's note says the last word of the chapter is doubtful, and one papyrus has Nebes, a lion-headed goddess.

long_description.id: Renouf menyatakan serangga yang disebut āpšai atau āpsȧit sulit diidentifikasi. Ia jelas bukan kura-kura seperti anggapan sebelumnya, tetapi lebih mirip Blatta orientalis yang rakus. Gambaran ini berbeda dari deskripsi kumbang besar pemakan daging pada sumber pertama.
long_description.en: Renouf says the insect called āpšai or āpsȧit is difficult to identify. It is certainly not a tortoise as formerly thought, but looks rather like the voracious Blatta orientalis. This differs from the description of a large flesh-eating beetle in the first source.

statement.id: Renouf menyatakan serangga yang disebut āpšai atau āpsȧit sulit diidentifikasi dan jelas bukan kura-kura seperti anggapan sebelumnya.
statement.en: Renouf states that the insect called āpšai or āpsȧit is difficult to identify and is certainly not a tortoise as formerly thought.

claims.quote: Chapter whereby the Āpshait is kept back.

statement.id: Bab XXXVI Kitab Orang Mati dalam terjemahan Renouf berjudul "Bab yang menahan Āpshait".
statement.en: Chapter XXXVI of the Book of the Dead in Renouf's translation is titled "Chapter whereby the Āpshait is kept back".

claims.quote: Chapter whereby the Āpshait is kept back. Away from me, thou with parted lips! I am Chnemu, the Lord of Shennu, who am bringing the words of the gods to Rā. And I announce the news to Nebes.

statement.id: Teks bab yang menahan Āpshait berbunyi "Pergilah dariku, kau yang berbibir terbuka! Akulah Chnemu, Tuan Shennu, yang membawa kata-kata para dewa kepada Rā. Dan aku mengumumkan kabar itu kepada Nebes."
statement.en: The text of the chapter whereby the Āpshait is kept back reads "Away from me, thou with parted lips! I am Chnemu, the Lord of Shennu, who am bringing the words of the gods to Rā. And I announce the news to Nebes."

claims.quote: The insect called āpšai or āpsȧit is difficult of identification. It is certainly not a tortoise as was formerly thought, but looks rather like the voracious Blatta orientalis.

statement.id: Renouf menilai serangga āpšai atau āpsȧit sulit diidentifikasi, jelas bukan kura-kura seperti anggapan sebelumnya, tetapi lebih mirip Blatta orientalis yang rakus.
statement.en: Renouf judges the insect āpšai or āpsȧit difficult to identify, certainly not a tortoise as formerly thought, but looking rather like the voracious Blatta orientalis.

claims.quote: The last word of the chapter is doubtful. The most recent papyri have ‘their Lord,’ which gives a very good sense, but even the Turin copy has ‘her Lord’ which agrees with the oldest papyrus. Bekenrenef has Nebes, a lion-headed goddess.

statement.id: Menurut catatan Renouf, kata terakhir bab itu meragukan: papirus terbaru memuat "Tuan mereka", salinan Turin dan papirus tertua memuat "Tuan perempuan itu", dan Bekenrenef memuat Nebes, dewi berkepala singa.
statement.en: According to Renouf's note, the last word of the chapter is doubtful: the most recent papyri have "their Lord", the Turin copy and the oldest papyrus have "her Lord", and Bekenrenef has Nebes, a lion-headed goddess.

summary.id: Wikipedia menjelaskannya sebagai kumbang besar pemakan daging.
summary.en: Wikipedia describes it as a large flesh-eating beetle.

summary.id: Renouf menolak kura-kura dan menilai serangga itu lebih mirip Blatta orientalis, dengan catatan identifikasinya sulit.
summary.en: Renouf rejects the tortoise and judges the insect more like Blatta orientalis, noting that identification is difficult.

short_description.id: Atago Gongen adalah kami sekaligus tengu dari Gunung Atago di Kyoto, perwujudan setempat Jizō dan Izanami, yang dipuja sebagai pelindung dari api serta dewa perang dan kemenangan.
short_description.en: Atago Gongen is a kami and tengu of Mount Atago in Kyoto, the local manifestation of Jizō and Izanami, venerated as a guardian against fire and as a deity of war and victory.

long_description.id: Atago Gongen (愛宕権現), juga disebut Tarōbō atau Shōgun Jizō, adalah kami dan tengu Gunung Atago. Ia dipercaya sebagai avatar setempat Bodhisattva Jizō dan dewi Shinto Izanami. Artikel berbahasa Jepang menyebutnya gelar ilahi sinkretis yang memadukan pemujaan gunung Atago dengan shugendō.
long_description.en: Atago Gongen (愛宕権現), also called Tarōbō or Shōgun Jizō, is a kami and tengu of Mount Atago. He is believed to be the local avatar of the bodhisattva Jizō and the Shinto goddess Izanami. The Japanese article calls him a syncretic divine title fusing mountain worship at Atago with shugendō.

long_description.id: Ia digambarkan menunggang kuda putih sambil membawa tongkat bergelang dan permata penghapus keinginan (desire-cancelling jewel), atau dalam rupa Shōgun Jizō berbaju zirah di atas kuda. Dalam satu legenda, tengu bernama Tarōbō menyerah kepada para resi dan menjadi pelindung gunung. Sebuah sumber menyebut keyakinan bahwa tengu Atago Tarōbō tinggal di gunung itu.
long_description.en: He is pictured on a white horse carrying a ringed staff and a desire-cancelling jewel, or as Shōgun Jizō in armor on horseback. In one legend the tengu named Tarōbō surrendered to the sages and became protector of the mountain. One source records the belief that the tengu Atago Tarōbō lived on the mountain.

long_description.id: Kami Atago dipuja sebagai pelindung dari bencana api, dan para prajurit memujanya sebagai dewa perang dan kemenangan. Jimat bertuliskan "hinoyōjin" dibagikan kepada anggota perkumpulan pemujanya, dan berziarah ke Kuil Atago pada hari pertama bulan kedelapan dipercaya setara dengan berziarah selama seribu hari. Pada tahun 1868, pemisahan Shinto dan Buddha menghapus Atago Gongen yang berbasis shugendō.
long_description.en: The kami of Atago was worshipped as a protector against fire disasters, and warriors honored him as a god of war and victory. Amulets bearing "hinoyōjin" were given to members of the confraternities devoted to him, and visiting Atago Shrine on the first day of the eighth month was believed to equal a thousand days of visits. In 1868 the separation of Shinto and Buddhism abolished the shugendō-based Atago Gongen.

claims.quote: Atago Gongen (愛宕権現) also known as Tarōbō (太郎坊), Atago Daigongen (愛宕大権現), Shōgun Jizō (勝軍地蔵) of Mount Atago is a Japanese kami and tengu believed to be the local avatar (Gongen) of Buddhist bodhisattva Jizō and Shinto goddess Izanami.

claims.quote: The kami of Atago has been worshipped as a protector against fire disasters. The mountain is located northwest of Kyōto from which direction thunder and lightning clouds often appear, which may explain the development of the kami's character as a "fire kami" (hi no kami).

statement.en: The kami of Atago has been worshipped as a protector against fire disasters; the mountain lies northwest of Kyōto, the direction thunder and lightning clouds often come from, which may explain the development of its character as a "fire kami" (hi no kami).

claims.quote: There is a belief that a tengu (a bird-like mythical creature) named Atago Tarōbō lived on the mountain, and the area flourished as a sacred shugendō site.

statement.id: Ada kepercayaan bahwa seekor tengu (makhluk mitos mirip burung) bernama Atago Tarōbō tinggal di gunung itu, dan kawasan itu berkembang sebagai tempat suci shugendō.
statement.en: There is a belief that a tengu (a bird-like mythical creature) named Atago Tarōbō lived on the mountain, and the area flourished as a sacred shugendō site.

claims.quote: Moreover, because Shōgun Jizō (the battle-victory Jizo Buddha) was worshipped as the Buddhist avatar (honji butsu) of Atago, the Atago kami was popular with the warrior class as a "military kami" (gunshin) in the medieval period.

statement.id: Karena Shōgun Jizō (Jizō pembawa kemenangan perang) dipuja sebagai avatar Buddhis Atago, kami Atago populer di kalangan kelas prajurit pada abad pertengahan sebagai "kami militer" (gunshin).
statement.en: Because Shōgun Jizō (the battle-victory Jizō Buddha) was worshipped as the Buddhist avatar (honji butsu) of Atago, the Atago kami was popular with the warrior class in the medieval period as a "military kami" (gunshin).

claims.quote: People in various regions established Atago-kō confraternities and members customarily received a shikimi branch and a "kami amulet" (shinsatsu) with the words "hinoyōjin" (a formula to protect one from fire) written on it.

statement.en: People in various regions founded Atago-kō confraternities; members customarily received a shikimi branch and a kami amulet (shinsatsu) bearing the words "hinoyōjin", a formula for protection from fire.

claims.quote: There was also the belief that visiting Atago Shrine on the first day of the eighth month, a visit known as "sennichi mōde" ("prayer of 1000 days merit"), generated the virtue equivalent of visiting the shrine every day for one thousand days.

statement.id: Ada pula kepercayaan bahwa berziarah ke Kuil Atago pada hari pertama bulan kedelapan ("sennichi mōde") menghasilkan pahala setara berziarah setiap hari selama seribu hari.
statement.en: There was also a belief that visiting Atago Shrine on the first day of the eighth month ("sennichi mōde") earned merit equal to visiting every day for a thousand days.

statement.en: During the Heian period Atago was counted among the "seven high mountains" (shichi kōsan) of the Kinki region.

statement.en: Atago Gongen is a syncretic Shinto-Buddhist divine title fusing mountain worship at Atago with shugendō, with Izanami as the manifested deity and Jizō Bodhisattva as the original Buddhist form.

short_description.id: Atlacoya adalah dewi kekeringan dalam mitologi Aztek (Mexica); namanya ditafsirkan sebagai "air yang sedih". Ia digambarkan bercakap dengan Mayahuel dalam sebuah kodeks.
short_description.en: Atlacoya is a goddess of drought in Aztec (Mexica) mythology; her name is glossed as "sad water". She is shown talking with Mayahuel in a codex.

long_description.id: Atlacoya, juga ditulis Atlacoaya, adalah dewi kekeringan dan air kotor dalam mitologi Mexica; namanya ditafsirkan sebagai "air yang sedih". Satu artikel menyebutnya dewi kekeringan dalam mitologi Aztek yang juga dewi pulque, sedangkan artikel lain menyebutnya dewa kekeringan dan tanah tandus. Satu sumber lain menempatkannya dalam mitologi Mixtek, juga sebagai dewi kekeringan.
long_description.en: Atlacoya, also spelled Atlacoaya, is the goddess of drought and dark waters in Mexica mythology; her name is glossed as "sad water". One article calls her an Aztec goddess of drought who is also a goddess of pulque, while another article calls her the deity (isten) of drought and infertile lands. Another source places her in Mixtec mythology, again as a drought goddess.

long_description.id: Penggambarannya yang paling terkenal ada di Codex Magliabechiano, tempat ia bercakap dengan Mayáhuel. Menurut salah satu artikel, hal itu tampak pada lembar 46 dan 63, dan keduanya memakai quechquemitl serta tunik tanpa lengan. Laba-laba Meksiko Scytodes atlacoya dinamai menurut dewi ini.
long_description.en: Her best-known image is in the Codex Magliabechiano, where she talks with Mayáhuel. According to one article this appears on folios 46 and 63, and both wear a quechquemitl and sleeveless tunics. The Mexican spider Scytodes atlacoya is named after her.

short_description.id: Ayao adalah orisha udara dalam panteon Santería, agama Karibia. Ia digambarkan sebagai pejuang garang yang berdiam di hutan dan di mata tornado, dan sering ditempatkan di samping saudarinya, Oya.
short_description.en: Ayao is the orisha of the air in the pantheon of Santería, a Caribbean religion. She is portrayed as a fierce warrior who dwells in the forest and in the eye of the tornado, and is often placed beside her sister Oya.

long_description.id: Ayao, yang dalam sumber kedua ditulis Aiaó, adalah orisha dalam panteon Santería atau Lucumi. Ia dipandang sebagai penguasa udara yang tinggal di hutan dan di pusat pusaran tornado. Ayao bekerja erat dengan Ọsanyìn dan dikenal sebagai pejuang yang garang.
long_description.en: Ayao, written Aiaó in the second source, is an orisha of the Santería or Lucumi pantheon. She is regarded as ruler of the air who lives in the forest and at the center of the tornado's whirl. Ayao works closely with Ọsanyìn and is known as a fierce warrior.

long_description.id: Perlengkapan Ayao meliputi senjata busur dengan ular, sebatang bulu pena, dan sembilan batu. Warnanya cokelat dan hijau, dan ia lazim diletakkan di samping saudarinya, Oya atau Oiá. Sebagian penganut bahkan memindahkan busur dan panah dari mahkota Oiá ke wadah milik Aiaó.
long_description.en: Ayao's implements include a bow-weapon bearing a serpent, a quill and nine stones. Her colors are brown and green, and she is usually set next to her sister, Oya or Oiá. Some devotees even move the bow and arrow from Oiá's crown into Aiaó's receptacle.

long_description.id: Pemujaan Ayao sempat dikira telah lenyap, tetapi kini makin banyak penganut yang memilikinya. Sumber kedua menyebut makin banyak inisiat menerimanya dalam kerasukan.
long_description.en: Ayao's cult was once believed to have vanished, yet a growing number of devotees now hold her. The second source says more and more initiates receive her during possession.
