description.en: The Bulgae always chase the Sun and Moon, and eclipses occur when they bite the celestial bodies.

name.id: Matahari terlalu panas dan bulan terlalu dingin
name.en: The sun is too hot and the moon too cold

description.id: Dalam kisah Gamangnara, Bulgae tidak dapat menahan Matahari yang terlalu panas dan menjatuhkan Bulan yang membuat mulutnya membeku, sehingga selalu gagal.
description.en: In the Gamangnara tale the Bulgae cannot hold the Sun, which is too hot, and drops the Moon, which freezes its mouth, so they always fail.

title.en: The king of Gamangnara and the fire dogs

role.id: Bulgae adalah anjing yang diutus mencuri matahari dan bulan.
role.en: The Bulgae are the dogs sent to steal the sun and moon.

summary.id: Raja negeri gelap Gamangnara mengutus anjing api raksasa mencuri Matahari lalu Bulan; semuanya gagal karena Matahari terlalu panas dan Bulan terlalu dingin, tetapi sang raja terus mengutus anjing yang lebih garang.
summary.en: The king of the dark world Gamangnara sends gigantic fire dogs to steal the Sun and then the Moon; all fail because the Sun is too hot and the Moon too cold, but the king keeps sending fiercer dogs.

description.id: Negeri kegelapan di langit tempat Bulgae berasal.
description.en: The kingdom of darkness in the heavens from which the Bulgae come.

claims.quote: refers to the mythical fire dogs in Korean mythology. They come from the kingdom of darkness and always chase the Sun and Moon, causing eclipses when they bite both the celestial bodies.

statement.id: Bulgae adalah anjing api mitologis Korea yang berasal dari kerajaan kegelapan.
statement.en: Bulgae are Korean mythological fire dogs from a kingdom of darkness.

claims.quote: refers to the mythical fire dogs in Korean mythology. They come from the kingdom of darkness and always chase the Sun and Moon, causing eclipses when they bite both the celestial bodies.

statement.id: Gigitan mereka terhadap matahari dan bulan menjelaskan gerhana dalam legenda.
statement.en: Their bites of the sun and moon explain eclipses in legend.

claims.quote: In Korean mythology, the cosmological narratives and legends such as the Isik, Wolsik legend, explain the eclipse phenomenon with the Bulgae dogs.

statement.id: Legenda Isik dan Wolsik menghubungkan fenomena gerhana dengan anjing Bulgae.
statement.en: The Isik and Wolsik legends link eclipse phenomena to Bulgae dogs.

claims.quote: According to the myth recorded in the Hangug-ui seolwo (Folk Myths from Korea), there were many realms of heaven. One of them, the kingdom of darkness, was called Gamangnara, the Dark World. The king of Gamangnara was concerned and weary with the darkness and desired the light of the Sun and Moon for his kingdom.

statement.id: Kisah Gamangnara menyebut raja negeri gelap mengirim anjing api untuk mengambil cahaya matahari.
statement.en: The Gamangnara tale describes its king sending a fiery hound to fetch sunlight.

claims.quote: He sent one of the gigantic fiery hounds, the Bulgae, belonging to one of his dark world subjects, to chase the Sun and bring it to his realm. However, when the Bulgae tried to bite the Sun, the Sun was too hot, which made the dog unable to hold on to it, resulting in him giving up, and running back to the king.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, raja mengirim salah satu anjing api raksasa, Bulgae, untuk mengejar Matahari dan membawanya ke negerinya, tetapi Matahari terlalu panas sehingga anjing itu tidak dapat menahannya, menyerah, dan lari kembali kepada raja.
statement.en: According to the article, the king sent one of the gigantic fiery hounds, the Bulgae, to chase the Sun and bring it to his realm, but the Sun was too hot for the dog to hold on to, so it gave up and ran back to the king.

claims.quote: In another attempt to get rid of the darkness he sent another more ruthless dog to steal the Moon. When the Bulgae tried to carry the Moon in its mouth, the Moon was so cold, that the mouth of the dog was icy and frozen, and caused the Bulgae to drop the Moon from its mouth.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, raja mengirim anjing lain yang lebih kejam untuk mencuri Bulan, tetapi Bulan begitu dingin sehingga mulut anjing itu membeku dan Bulgae menjatuhkan Bulan dari mulutnya.
statement.en: According to the article, the king sent another, more ruthless dog to steal the Moon, but the Moon was so cold that the dog's mouth froze and the Bulgae dropped the Moon from its mouth.

claims.quote: He continued to send fire dogs that were fiercer than the others, but none were able to collect the Sun and Moon. According to the Korean eclipse belief, during a solar eclipse or lunar eclipse, the dark sections are the parts where the dogs are biting. When the eclipses are over, the dogs have given up and run away back to Gamangnara.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, raja terus mengirim anjing api yang makin garang tetapi tidak ada yang berhasil mengambil Matahari dan Bulan; menurut kepercayaan gerhana Korea, bagian gelap saat gerhana adalah bagian yang digigit anjing-anjing itu, dan setelah gerhana usai mereka menyerah dan kembali ke Gamangnara.
statement.en: According to the article, the king kept sending ever fiercer fire dogs but none could collect the Sun and Moon; in the Korean eclipse belief, the dark sections during an eclipse are where the dogs are biting, and when the eclipse is over the dogs give up and run back to Gamangnara.

claims.quote: Bulgae are strong and fierce dogs or hairy dogs which are likely to be the indigenous Korean dog breed Sapsali, which means "ghost chasing dog".

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, Bulgae adalah anjing kuat dan garang atau anjing berbulu yang kemungkinan adalah anjing asli Korea, Sapsali, yang berarti "anjing pengejar hantu".
statement.en: According to the article, Bulgae are strong and fierce dogs, or hairy dogs, likely the indigenous Korean dog breed Sapsali, meaning "ghost chasing dog".

claims.quote: 가막나라의 임금은 나라가 어두운 것을 걱정하여, 백성들이 기르던 사나운 불개를 불러 해와 달을 훔쳐오라고 하였다.

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Korea menyebut raja Gamak-nara (가막나라), karena cemas negerinya gelap, memanggil Bulgae (불개) ganas milik rakyatnya dan menyuruhnya mencuri matahari dan bulan.
statement.en: Korean Wikipedia says the king of Gamak-nara (가막나라), worried that his country was dark, summoned the fierce Bulgae (불개) kept by his people and told them to steal the sun and the moon.

claims.quote: 이렇게 불개들이 해와 달을 물 때마다 그 부분이 어둡게 보였고, 일식과 월식이 가막나라의 불개 때문에 생긴다고 전해진다.

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Korea menyebut bahwa setiap kali Bulgae menggigit matahari dan bulan bagian itu tampak gelap, dan gerhana matahari dan bulan konon terjadi karena Bulgae dari Gamak-nara.
statement.en: Korean Wikipedia says that each time the Bulgae bit the sun and moon that part looked dark, and solar and lunar eclipses are said to be caused by the Bulgae of Gamak-nara.

claims.quote: 1930년 발간된 손진태의 《조선민담집》(朝鮮民譚集)에서는 〈일식과 월식〉이라는 이름으로 위 이야기를 1923년 함흥에서 채록한 것으로 기록하였으며

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Korea mencatat bahwa kisah ini dimuat dalam Joseon Mindamjip (1930) karya Son Jin-tae dengan judul "Gerhana Matahari dan Bulan", dikumpulkan di Hamhung pada 1923.
statement.en: Korean Wikipedia records that this tale appears in Son Jin-tae's Joseon Mindamjip (1930) under the title "Solar and Lunar Eclipses", collected in Hamhung in 1923.

claims.quote: 1952년 발간된 정인섭의 《한국의 설화》(Folktales from Korea)에 수록된 〈불개〉(The Fire Dogs)는 1912년 언양에서 채록한 것으로 원전을 밝히고 있다. 임석재(任晳宰, 1903~1998)의 《한국구전설화》(韓國口傳說話)에서는 1915년 순창에서 채록본을 수록하고 있다.

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Korea mencatat bahwa "Bulgae" (The Fire Dogs) dalam Folktales from Korea (1952) karya Jeong In-seop dicatat berasal dari Eonyang pada 1912, dan Hanguk Gujeon Seolhwa karya Im Seok-jae memuat versi dari Sunchang tahun 1915.
statement.en: Korean Wikipedia records that "Bulgae" (The Fire Dogs) in Jeong In-seop's Folktales from Korea (1952) is stated to be collected in Eonyang in 1912, and Im Seok-jae's Hanguk Gujeon Seolhwa includes a version collected in Sunchang in 1915.

short_description.id: Burha dangoria adalah kekuatan supranatural dalam kepercayaan rakyat Assam yang dipandang dengan hormat dan rasa takut.
short_description.en: Burha dangoria is a supernatural power in Assamese folk belief regarded with respect and fear.

long_description.id: Burha dangoria adalah kekuatan supranatural dalam kepercayaan rakyat Assam yang dipandang dengan hormat dan rasa takut. Ia digambarkan sebagai sosok laki-laki tampan, bukan makhluk berwujud menakutkan.
long_description.en: Burha dangoria is a supernatural power in Assamese folk belief regarded with respect and fear. He is portrayed as a handsome man rather than a terrifying being.

long_description.id: Ia dipercaya tinggal di pohon-pohon tinggi. Dalam penggambaran, ia memakai pakaian putih dan menunggang kuda. Menebang pohon tempat tinggalnya atau meremehkannya dipercaya mengundang kemarahannya. Orang mengadakan nyanyian keagamaan di bawah pohon dan menjaga kebersihannya.
long_description.en: He is believed to dwell in tall trees. In depictions he wears white clothing and rides a horse. Cutting his dwelling tree or belittling him is believed to provoke his anger. People hold religious singing beneath the tree and keep it clean.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah buku tentang roh-roh Assam, Rajkhowa menyebut bura-dangaria sebagai gelar hormat bagi pria Assam lanjut usia. Roh ini digambarkan tinggi, kekar, tampak seperti mawar yang mekar penuh, dan di antara semua roh dikatakan paling religius. Orang yang menebang pohon yang dihuninya tanpa menenangkannya dihukum dengan penyakit badan.
long_description.en: In a book on Assamese spirits, Rajkhowa calls bura-dangaria a title of respect for an elderly Assamese gentleman. The spirit is described as tall, strongly built and looking like a full-blossomed rose, and of all the spirits is said to be the most religiously disposed. Those who fell a tree haunted by it without propitiating it are scourged with bodily ailments.

short_description.id: Caacrinolaas atau Glasya-Labolas adalah Presiden neraka dalam demonologi, anjing bersayap griffin yang menghasut pertumpahan darah.
short_description.en: Caacrinolaas or Glasya-Labolas is a President of hell in demonology, a griffin-winged dog who incites bloodshed.

long_description.id: Caacrinolaas, lebih dikenal sebagai Glasya-Labolas, adalah Presiden neraka yang memimpin tiga puluh enam legiun iblis. Ia digambarkan sebagai anjing bersayap griffin. Ia dapat memberi bakat seni rupa tetapi juga membangkitkan haus darah, menjadi biang pembunuhan, mengetahui masa lalu dan masa depan, menimbulkan cinta antara kawan dan lawan, dan membuat orang tidak terlihat.
long_description.en: Caacrinolaas, better known as Glasya-Labolas, is a President of hell commanding thirty-six legions of demons. He is depicted as a dog with griffin's wings. He can grant talent in the fine arts but also inspire bloodlust, is the author of murders, knows past and future, causes love between friends and foes, and can make a man invisible.

long_description.id: Sebuah kamus demonologi menyebutnya "Caacrinolaas", juga disebut Caassimolar dan Glassialabolas, presiden agung di neraka yang tampil sebagai anjing dengan sayap griffon. Ia memberi pengetahuan tentang seni-seni liberal tetapi juga mengilhami pembunuhan, dikatakan meramalkan masa depan dengan baik, membuat manusia tak terlihat, dan memimpin tiga puluh enam legiun. Le Grand Grimoire menyebutnya Classyalabolas dan hanya menjadikannya semacam sersan yang kadang menjadi tunggangan Nébiros atau Naberus.
long_description.en: A demonological dictionary calls him "Caacrinolaas", also called Caassimolar and Glassialabolas, a great president in hell who appears as a dog with griffin's wings. He gives knowledge of the liberal arts but also inspires homicides, is said to predict the future well, makes a man invisible and commands thirty-six legions. The Grand Grimoire calls him Classyalabolas and makes him only a kind of sergeant who sometimes serves as a mount for Nébiros or Naberus.

short_description.id: Canterbury Panther adalah legenda urban New Zealand tentang panther hitam yang konon hidup di wilayah Canterbury, dengan laporan penampakan sejak sebelum 1970-an.
short_description.en: The Canterbury Panther is a New Zealand urban legend about a black panther said to live in the Canterbury Region, with sightings reported since before the 1970s.

long_description.id: Canterbury Panther atau Canterbury Cat adalah legenda urban New Zealand tentang panther hitam yang konon hidup di wilayah Canterbury. Penampakan hewan itu tercatat sejak sebelum 1970-an.
long_description.en: The Canterbury Panther, also called the Canterbury Cat, is a New Zealand urban legend of a black panther said to inhabit the Canterbury Region; sightings are reported from before the 1970s.

long_description.id: Legenda ini pertama kali menjadi berita utama pada Juli 1977, ketika warga Kaiapoi, Frances Clark, mengaku melihat seekor harimau di luar rumahnya. Clark mula-mula tidak dipercaya, sampai jejak kaki besar dan kotoran besar ditemukan di pantai terdekat; pencarian lewat darat dan udara tidak menemukan kucing raksasa. Kemudian, seorang perempuan melaporkan kucing hitam "sebesar Labrador" pada 1996 dan penampakan panther hitam dilaporkan di Mackenzie Country pada 1999.
long_description.en: The legend first reached the headlines in July 1977, when Frances Clark of Kaiapoi claimed to have seen a tiger outside her house. At first she was discredited, until large paw prints and droppings turned up on a nearby beach; a search by land and air found no giant cat. Later, a woman reported a black cat "the size of a Labrador" in 1996 and a sighting of a black panther was said to have been seen in Mackenzie Country in 1999.

long_description.id: Penjelasan yang paling umum mengaitkan penampakan itu dengan salah identifikasi kucing liar berbulu hitam yang luar biasa besar. Seorang penulis NZ Skeptics menilai tidak ada bukti yang dapat diverifikasi dan menyimpulkan bahwa panther itu mungkin hanya gabungan salah identifikasi, pembuatan mitos, dan kekuatan sugesti.
long_description.en: The commonest explanation blames mistaken identity of unusually big feral cats with black coats. An NZ Skeptics author finds no verifiable proof and concludes the panther may be merely a mix of mis-identifications, myth-making and suggestion.

long_description.id: Sang panther juga menjadi tambahan bagi film petualangan keluarga Timpson, Bookworm.
long_description.en: The panther also became an addition to Timpson's family adventure film Bookworm.

short_description.id: Chalchiuhtlicue adalah dewi Aztec untuk danau, aliran air, kesuburan, dan persalinan, yang juga dianggap melindungi perempuan dan anak-anak.
short_description.en: Chalchiuhtlicue is the Aztec goddess of lakes and streams, fertility, and childbirth, thought to protect women and children.

long_description.id: Chalchiuhtlicue adalah dewi danau dan aliran air dalam agama Aztec. Ia dikaitkan dengan kesuburan, menjadi pelindung persalinan, dan termasuk kelompok besar dewa hujan Aztec yang berkerabat dengan dewa air Chalchiuhtlatonal. Bersama Tlaloc, ia disebut membantu memerintah kerajaan firdaus Tlalocan.
long_description.en: Chalchiuhtlicue is the Aztec goddess of lakes and streams. She is linked with fertility, acts as patroness of childbirth, and belongs to a larger group of Aztec rain gods closely related to the water god Chalchiuhtlatonal. Together with Tlaloc she is said to help rule the paradisial kingdom of Tlalocan.

long_description.id: Ia membawa kesuburan bagi tanaman dan diyakini melindungi perempuan serta anak-anak; ia juga disebut penjaga bayi baru lahir. Selain itu ia memimpin ritus kelahiran, pemandian korban persembahan, penyucian peradilan, dan penobatan raja. Dalam sebuah gambar, cangkang kerang di tepi air menunjukkan kaitannya dengan kesuburan. Sumber-sumber berbeda menyebutnya istri atau saudari Tlaloc, dan dalam teks lain istri Xiuhtecuhtli.
long_description.en: Crops gain fertility through her, and women and children are believed to be under her protection; she is also called the guardian of newborns. In addition she presided over birth rituals, the bathing of sacrificial victims, judicial purification, and royal investiture. In one picture, seashells at the water's edge point to her link with fertility. Sources differ on whether she was wife or sister of Tlaloc, and other texts make her the wife of Xiuhtecuhtli.

long_description.id: Menurut mitos ia pernah memakan matahari dan bulan, dan ia sering dikaitkan dengan ular. Dalam mitos Lima Matahari ia memimpin Matahari Keempat dan diyakini menghancurkannya dengan hujan selama 52 tahun sebagai balasan atas perlakuan buruk Tlaloc. Kalender Aztec memuat lima perayaan besar bagi dirinya dan Tlaloc, ketika para imam menyelam ke danau dan menirukan katak. Dalam seni ia sering dipahat dari batu hijau sesuai namanya, yang paling lazim ditafsirkan sebagai "dia yang berok batu giok".
long_description.en: Myths say she once ate the sun and the moon, and she is often associated with serpents. In the Five Suns myth she presided over the Fourth Sun and is believed to have destroyed it with 52 years of rain in retaliation for Tlaloc's mistreatment. The Aztec calendar held five big celebrations for her and Tlaloc, during which priests dove into a lake and imitated frogs. In sculpture she is often carved from green stone, in keeping with her name, which is most commonly read as "she of the jade skirt".

cultural_context.id: Lima dari 20 perayaan besar dalam kalender Aztec dipersembahkan bagi dirinya dan Tlaloc; pada perayaan itu para imam menyelam ke danau dan menirukan katak untuk memohon hujan. Ia juga dipuja khusus oleh para pembawa air.
cultural_context.en: Of the 20 great festivals of the Aztec calendar, five honoured her together with Tlaloc, and on them priests dived into a lake and mimicked frogs to coax rain; water-carriers also worshipped her in a special way.

short_description.id: Chessie adalah monster laut dalam cerita rakyat Amerika yang konon hidup di Teluk Chesapeake. Digambarkan menyerupai ular raksasa, ia kini juga menjadi ikon lingkungan teluk itu.
short_description.en: Chessie is an American folklore sea monster said to live in Chesapeake Bay. Described as a giant snake-like creature, it has also become an environmental icon of the bay.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Amerika, Chessie adalah monster laut yang konon hidup di Teluk Chesapeake. Laporan penampakan muncul di media lokal dan buku bertema kedaerahan sejak 1936. Menurut laporan yang dihimpun sebuah proyek penyelidik, makhluk ini berulang kali digambarkan menyerupai ular, sekitar dua puluh lima sampai empat puluh kaki panjangnya, berkepala elips atau seperti bola football.
long_description.en: Chessie is a sea monster of American folklore, said to dwell in the Chesapeake Bay. Reports of sightings have been printed in local media and regional books since 1936. According to reports gathered by an investigative project, the creature is repeatedly described as serpentine, about twenty-five to forty feet long, with an elliptical or football-shaped head.

long_description.id: Menurut penulis sebuah halaman web universitas, ketenaran Chessie baru benar-benar muncul pada 1978, ketika surat kabar Virginia mulai memuat laporan penampakan. Pada 31 Mei 1982, Robert Frew, warga Maryland, merekam video makhluk menyerupai ular yang berenang sekitar 100 kaki dari dermaga rumahnya di Kent Island. Ilmuwan Smithsonian yang memeriksa rekaman itu tidak dapat menarik kesimpulan apa pun. Artikel Wikipedia juga mencatat bahwa penampakan helikopter 1936 tampak tidak mungkin, dan sketsa September 1980 kemudian diidentifikasi sebagai manatee dari Florida.
long_description.en: According to the author of a university web page, Chessie's notoriety only really surfaced in 1978, when Virginia newspapers began printing sightings. On May 31, 1982, Maryland resident Robert Frew videotaped a serpent-like creature swimming about 100 feet off the bulkhead of his Kent Island home. Smithsonian scientists who examined the tape could reach no conclusions. The Wikipedia article also notes that the 1936 helicopter sighting seems unlikely, and that a September 1980 sketch was later identified as a manatee from Florida.

long_description.id: Seiring waktu, Chessie berkembang menjadi ikon lingkungan yang dikaitkan dengan kesehatan ekologi Teluk Chesapeake. Pada 1986 Dinas Perikanan dan Margasatwa AS memakainya dalam buku mewarnai edukatif Chessie: A Chesapeake Bay Story.
long_description.en: Over time, Chessie developed into an environmental icon associated with the ecological health of Chesapeake Bay. In 1986 the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service used it in its educational coloring book Chessie: A Chesapeake Bay Story.

text.en: The term originated in China roughly 2,500 years ago in ancient chronicles such as the Zuo Zhuan

short_description.id: Chimimōryō (Tiongkok: chimei wangliang) adalah istilah untuk monster atau roh gunung dan sungai, yang berasal dari tulisan Tiongkok kuno dan kemudian dipakai dalam bahasa Jepang untuk beragam yōkai.
short_description.en: Chimimōryō (Chinese: chimei wangliang) is a term for the monsters or spirits of mountains and rivers, originating in ancient Chinese writings and later used in Japanese for various yōkai.

long_description.id: Chimimōryō (Tiongkok: chimei wangliang; 魑魅魍魎) adalah istilah yang merujuk pada monster gunung dan monster sungai. Istilah ini berasal dari Tiongkok sekitar 2.500 tahun lalu dalam kronik kuno seperti Zuo Zhuan, dan berakar pada legenda kuno tentang roh yang mencelakai orang di gunung dan rawa; arti aslinya adalah "segala jenis yaoguai (iblis dan hantu)".
long_description.en: Chimimōryō (Chinese: chimei wangliang; 魑魅魍魎) names the monsters of the mountains and the monsters of the rivers. The term arose in China some 2,500 years ago in early chronicles such as the Zuo Zhuan, and derives from ancient Chinese legends about spirits that harm people in the mountains and swamps; it originally meant "all kinds of yaoguai (demons and ghosts)".

long_description.id: Istilah ini terdiri dari dua unsur. Chimi disebut monster yang lahir dari hawa aneh hutan gunung, berwajah manusia dan bertubuh binatang, yang menyesatkan orang. Mōryō (wangliang) dianggap roh sungai, pohon, dan batu yang lahir dari hawa benda-benda alam dan menipu manusia; ia konon berwujud seperti anak kecil berkulit merah kehitaman bermata merah, bertelinga panjang, dan berambut indah.
long_description.en: The term has two components. Chimi is said to be a monster born of the strange vapors of mountain forests, with a human face and an animal body, that leads people astray. Mōryō (wangliang) are regarded as spirits of rivers, trees and rocks, born of the vital energy of natural things, that bewitch people; they are said to look like small children with dark red skin, red eyes, long ears and beautiful hair.

long_description.id: Dalam teks Zuo Zhuan, jawaban Wang Sunman kepada Pangeran Chu menyebut bahwa orang yang memasuki sungai, rawa, gunung, dan hutan tidak bertemu hal yang merugikan, dan 螭魅罔兩 tidak dapat menjumpai mereka. Heibonsha mencatat bahwa roh-roh ini bersifat lokal sehingga bertemu mereka tanpa persiapan dianggap berbahaya. Dalam bahasa Jepang modern, istilah ini juga dipakai untuk orang yang tak jelas jati dirinya.
long_description.en: In the Zuo Zhuan text, Wang Sunman's reply to the Prince of Chu says that people entering rivers, marshes, mountains and forests would not meet harmful things, and 螭魅罔兩 could not meet them. Heibonsha notes that these are local spirits, so meeting them without preparation was considered dangerous. In modern Japanese the term is also used for people who are inscrutable.

literal_meaning.id: Gabungan 魑魅 (chimei) dan 魍魎 (wangliang); ditulis juga 魑魅罔両, yang tampaknya bentuk aslinya.
literal_meaning.en: A compound of 魑魅 (chimei) and 魍魎 (wangliang); also written 魑魅罔両, which seems to be the original form.

who.id: Istilah untuk monster atau roh gunung dan sungai.
who.en: A term for monsters or spirits of mountains and rivers.

origin.id: Berasal dari tulisan Tiongkok kuno seperti Zuo Zhuan, kemudian dipakai dalam bahasa Jepang.
origin.en: Originates in ancient Chinese writings such as the Zuo Zhuan, later used in Japanese.

role.id: Dalam legenda kuno, roh-roh ini mencelakai orang di gunung dan rawa.
role.en: In ancient legends these spirits harm people in the mountains and swamps.

famous_for.id: Dikenal sebagai istilah umum untuk segala jenis makhluk gaib.
famous_for.en: Known as a general term for all kinds of supernatural beings.

name.en: Leading people astray and bewitching them

description.id: Chimi dikatakan menyesatkan orang dan mōryō menipu manusia.
description.en: Chimi is said to lead people astray and mōryō to bewitch people.

description.id: Mōryō konon takut harimau dan dapat dihindari dengan menaruh patung harimau dan pohon cemara.
description.en: Mōryō is said to fear tigers and can be avoided by placing a tiger image and cypress.

note.id: Arti asli istilah ini adalah "segala jenis yaoguai (iblis dan hantu)".
note.en: The original meaning of the term is "all kinds of yaoguai (demons and ghosts)".

note.id: 『和名類聚抄』 menggolongkan chimi sebagai sejenis oni bernama sudama, dan Heibonsha menyebut jenis kodama dan sudama.
note.en: The 『和名類聚抄』 classes chimi as a kind of oni called sudama, and Heibonsha refers to the kind of kodama and sudama.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa satu istilah dapat dipakai untuk menamai begitu banyak jenis makhluk gaib?
learning_questions.en: Why might a single term be used for so many kinds of supernatural beings?

sources.title: 王孫滿對楚子 (《左傳》宣公三年)

claims.quote: Chimei wangliang, or Chimimōryō (Chinese: 魑魅魍魉; pinyin: Chīmèi wǎngliǎng; Japanese: 魑魅魍魎 [ちみもうりょう]; rōmaji: chimimōryō), is a term that refers to monsters of the mountains and monsters of the rivers.

statement.id: Chimimōryō adalah istilah bagi makhluk gaib pegunungan dan perairan.
statement.en: Chimimōryō is a term for supernatural beings of mountains and waterways.

claims.quote: The term originated in China roughly 2,500 years ago in ancient chronicles such as the Zuo Zhuan.

statement.id: Istilah ini berasal dari tulisan Tiongkok kuno.
statement.en: The term originates in ancient Chinese writings.

claims.quote: It originates from ancient Chinese legends about the spirits that harm people in the mountains and swamps, and its original meaning is "all kinds of Yaoguai (demons and ghosts)".

statement.id: Legenda lama menggambarkan roh-roh tersebut membahayakan manusia.
statement.en: Older legends portray such spirits as harmful to people.

claims.quote: Wangliang (魍魎; mōryō in Japanese) are considered to be spirits from mountains and rivers, and trees and rocks.

statement.id: Wangliang (魍魎; mōryō dalam bahasa Jepang), salah satu unsur istilah itu, dianggap roh dari gunung dan sungai, serta pohon dan batu.
statement.en: Wangliang (魍魎; mōryō in Japanese), one component of the term, are considered to be spirits from mountains and rivers, and trees and rocks.

claims.quote: 魑魅魍魎（ちみもうりょう）とは、山の怪物や川の怪物。様々な妖怪変化。魑魅は山の怪、魍魎は川の怪であり、一般には山河全ての怪として魑魅魍魎の名で用いられることが多い。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang: 魑魅魍魎 (chimi-mōryō) adalah monster gunung dan monster sungai serta beragam yōkai; chimi adalah makhluk gaib gunung dan mōryō makhluk gaib sungai, dan nama ini umumnya dipakai untuk semua makhluk gaib gunung dan sungai.
statement.en: Japanese Wikipedia: 魑魅魍魎 (chimi-mōryō) means monsters of mountains and monsters of rivers, and various yōkai; chimi are mountain apparitions and mōryō river apparitions, and the name is commonly used for all the apparitions of mountains and rivers.

claims.quote: 魑魅とは、山林の異気（瘴気）から生ずるという怪物のことといわれている。顔は人間、体は獣の姿をしていて、人を迷わせる。平安時代中期の辞書『和名類聚抄』ではスダマという和名の鬼の一種とされ、江戸時代の百科事典『和漢三才図会』では山の神とされる。

statement.id: Chimi disebut monster yang lahir dari hawa aneh hutan gunung, berwajah manusia dan bertubuh binatang, serta menyesatkan orang; 『和名類聚抄』 zaman Heian menggolongkannya sejenis oni bernama sudama, dan 『和漢三才図会』 zaman Edo menyebutnya dewa gunung.
statement.en: Chimi is said to be a monster born of the strange vapors of mountain forests, with a human face and an animal body, that leads people astray; the Heian-period dictionary 『和名類聚抄』 classes it as a kind of oni called sudama, and the Edo-period encyclopedia 『和漢三才図会』 calls it a mountain god.

claims.quote: 魍魎は川や木石の精霊とされる。山・水・木・石などあらゆる自然物の精気から生じ、人を化かす。また、死者を食べるとも言われ、姿かたちは幼児に似ていて、2本足で立ち、赤黒色の皮膚をして、目は赤く、耳は長く、美しい髪と人に似た声をしている。

statement.id: Mōryō dianggap roh sungai, pohon, dan batu; ia lahir dari hawa semua benda alam dan menipu manusia, konon memakan orang mati, berwujud seperti anak kecil yang berdiri dengan dua kaki, berkulit merah kehitaman, bermata merah, bertelinga panjang, berambut indah, dan bersuara seperti manusia.
statement.en: Mōryō are regarded as spirits of rivers, trees and rocks; they arise from the vital energy of all natural things and bewitch people, are said to eat the dead, and look like young children standing on two legs, with dark red skin, red eyes, long ears, beautiful hair and a human-like voice.

claims.quote: 『和漢三才図会』では水神、古代中国の書『春秋左氏伝』では水沢の神とされる。虎を恐れるとされ、虎の像と柏を置いておくと避けられる。

statement.id: Dalam 『和漢三才図会』 mōryō adalah dewa air, dan dalam 『春秋左氏伝』 dewa rawa; ia konon takut harimau dan dapat dihindari dengan menaruh patung harimau dan pohon cemara.
statement.en: In 『和漢三才図会』 mōryō is a water god and in the 『春秋左氏伝』 a god of marshes; it is said to fear tigers and can be avoided by placing a tiger image and cypress.

claims.quote: 語源に関しては諸説あるが、古代中国の妖怪か精の一種とされる。『史記』（五帝本紀）によると、魑は虎の形をした山神、魅は猪頭人形の沢神とされ、ここから色々な獣の属性を併せ持った怪物のイメージが膨らんだ、と推測される。

statement.id: Asal kata punya banyak teori; menurut 『史記』 (Lima Kaisar), 魑 adalah dewa gunung berbentuk harimau dan 魅 dewa rawa berkepala babi hutan bertubuh manusia, dari sini diduga muncul citra monster berbagai sifat hewan.
statement.en: Etymology has many theories; according to the 『史記』 (Annals of the Five Emperors), 魑 is a tiger-shaped mountain god and 魅 a swamp god with a boar head and human form, from which the image of a monster combining various beasts' traits is surmised to have grown.

claims.quote: ( 「魑魅」は山林の気から生じるばけもの、「魍魎」は山川や木石の精霊 ) いろいろな妖怪変化。種々のばけもの。
claims.locator: 精選版 日本国語大辞典

statement.id: Nihon Kokugo Daijiten: 「魑魅」 adalah makhluk gaib yang lahir dari hawa gunung dan hutan, dan 「魍魎」 roh gunung, sungai, pohon, dan batu; secara umum berarti beragam yōkai.
statement.en: Nihon Kokugo Daijiten: 「魑魅」 is a monster born of the vapors of mountains and forests and 「魍魎」 a spirit of mountains, rivers, trees and rocks; together the word means various yōkai.

claims.quote: 中国の《左伝》の注に〈魑魅は山川の異気の生む所にして人に害をなすもの〉
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典

statement.id: Heibonsha: catatan atas 《左伝》 Tiongkok menyatakan bahwa 魑魅 adalah sesuatu yang lahir dari hawa aneh gunung dan sungai dan mencelakai orang.
statement.en: Heibonsha: a note to China's 《左伝》 says that 魑魅 is something born of the strange vapors of mountains and rivers that harms people.

claims.quote: これらは地方的な精霊であるため，中央集権的な神々の体制には服さず，それゆえ，人々が何の準備もなくこうした精霊と遭遇するのは危険であるとされた。
claims.locator: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典

statement.id: Heibonsha: karena roh-roh ini bersifat lokal dan tidak tunduk pada tatanan dewa yang tersentralisasi, bertemu mereka tanpa persiapan dianggap berbahaya.
statement.en: Heibonsha: since these are local spirits that do not submit to the centralized order of gods, meeting them without any preparation was considered dangerous.

claims.quote: 「魑魅罔両」とも書き、こちらのほうが本来のようです。でも、熟語としては、四字とも字形をそろえた「魑魅魍魎」が多く使われます。

statement.id: Kotobank: istilah ini juga ditulis 「魑魅罔両」, yang tampaknya bentuk aslinya, tetapi sebagai idiom lebih banyak dipakai 「魑魅魍魎」 dengan keempat karakter berbentuk serasi.
statement.en: Kotobank: the phrase is also written 「魑魅罔両」, which seems to be the original form, but as an idiom 「魑魅魍魎」, with all four characters given a matching form, is used more often.

claims.quote: では「魑」は山の神、「魅」は怪物、「魍魎」は水の神と説明します。他の書物ではまた説明が違うので、あまり厳密に考えなくてもかまわないでしょう。

statement.id: Kotobank: menurut penjelasan 「春秋左氏伝」, 「魑」 adalah dewa gunung, 「魅」 monster, dan 「魍魎」 dewa air; kitab lain menjelaskannya berbeda sehingga tak perlu dipahami terlalu ketat.
statement.en: Kotobank: in the 「春秋左氏伝」 explanation, 「魑」 is a mountain god, 「魅」 a monster and 「魍魎」 a water god; other books explain it differently, so it need not be taken too strictly.

claims.quote: 現代日本語で「魑魅魍魎」と言えば、単なるばけものではなく、多くは、ばけもののように得体の知れない人間たちを指します。

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Jepang modern, 「魑魅魍魎」 sering tidak lagi berarti sekadar makhluk gaib, melainkan orang-orang yang tak jelas jati dirinya seperti makhluk gaib.
statement.en: In modern Japanese, 「魑魅魍魎」 often no longer means mere monsters but people who are as inscrutable as monsters.

claims.quote: 昔夏之方有德也，遠方圖物，貢金九牧，鑄鼎象物，百物而為之備，使民知神姦。故民入川澤山林，不逢不若，螭魅罔兩，莫能逢之。

statement.id: Teks Zuo Zhuan (jawaban Wang Sunman kepada Pangeran Chu): ketika Xia berbudi, tripod dicetak dengan gambar segala hal agar rakyat mengenali yang gaib dan merugikan; maka orang yang memasuki sungai, rawa, gunung, dan hutan tidak bertemu hal yang merugikan, dan 螭魅罔兩 tidak dapat menjumpai mereka.
statement.en: Zuo Zhuan text (Wang Sunman's reply to the Prince of Chu): when Xia had virtue, tripods were cast with images of things so that the people would know the spirits and the harmful; so people entering rivers, marshes, mountains and forests would not meet harmful things, and 螭魅罔兩 could not meet them.

claims.quote: 定王使王孫滿勞楚子。楚子問鼎之大小輕重焉。對曰：「在德不在鼎。

statement.id: Konteksnya: Raja Ding mengutus Wang Sunman menyambut Pangeran Chu; sang pangeran menanyakan ukuran dan berat tripod, dan dijawab bahwa yang menentukan adalah kebajikan, bukan tripod.
statement.en: Context: King Ding sent Wang Sunman to receive the Prince of Chu; the prince asked about the size and weight of the tripods, and was answered that what matters is virtue, not the tripods.

short_description.id: Chinny-kinik adalah raksasa kanibal mengerikan dari mitologi Australian Aboriginal yang meneror dataran Yenpulla di South Australia [chinny-kinik-c01].
short_description.en: Chinny-kinik was a cannibal giant from Australian Aboriginal mythology who terrorized the Yenpulla plain in South Australia [chinny-kinik-c01].

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Australian Aboriginal di South Australia, Chinny-kinik adalah sosok raksasa pemangsa manusia yang meneror dataran Yenpulla di sebelah timur Murray River [chinny-kinik-c01]. Dua orang pamannya melacak jejaknya hingga ke lubang runtuhan di wilayah Pekarra dan menemukan pintu masuk ke gua yang luas [chinny-kinik-c02].
long_description.en: In Australian Aboriginal lore from South Australia, Chinny-kinik was a dreaded cannibal giant who terrorized the Yenpulla plain east of the Murray River [chinny-kinik-c01]. Two of his uncles tracked him to a sinkhole in Pekarra, discovering his cavernous hideout [chinny-kinik-c02].

long_description.id: Saat Chinny-kinik berlindung di dalam gua dari hembusan angin dingin, kedua pamannya menumpuk kayu bakar di mulut gua lalu menyalakannya [chinny-kinik-c03]. Mereka menambahkan batang kayu besar untuk menutup pintu masuk dan mengakhiri riwayat sang raksasa kanibal [chinny-kinik-c04].
long_description.en: While the giant took shelter inside against cold winds, the uncles piled firewood across the cave mouth and ignited it [chinny-kinik-c03]. Adding heavy logs to seal the blaze, they blocked the passage and secured his demise [chinny-kinik-c04].

long_description.id: Menurut sebuah jurnal speleologi, Tom Bellchambers mencatat legenda ini pada 1921. Chinny-kinik berkeliaran di dataran luas berhutan mallee di sebelah timur Murray River dan melahap siapa pun yang ia temui, sampai dua pamannya melacak jejak kakinya ke lubang runtuhan di Pekarra. Perjuangan dahsyatnya mengguncang bumi saat asap menyusup ke sarangnya.
long_description.en: A speleological journal reports that Tom Bellchambers recorded this legend in 1921. Chinny-kinik ranged across a wide mallee plain east of the Murray River, eating whoever he found, until two of his uncles followed his footprints to a sinkhole at Pekarra. His great struggles made the earth shake as smoke drifted into his lair.

long_description.id: Bellchambers bertekad menemukan gua itu dan mempersempit lokasinya ke bentang lima puluh kilometer di Murray Mallee bagian barat. Penulis artikel menduga nama "Pekarra" keliru dicatat dan seharusnya "Bakara", karena sebagian penutur Aborigin tidak membedakan bunyi p dan b. Gua Bakara Well baru ditemukan Wayne Goedecke pada awal 1970-an, dan penulis menilai lubang runtuhan serta parit yang mengarah ke pintu masuknya sesuai dengan deskripsi legenda.
long_description.en: Bellchambers set out to find the cave and narrowed its probable site to a fifty-kilometre strip of the western Murray Mallee. The article's author suggests "Pekarra" was misrecorded and should read "Bakara", since some Aboriginal speakers did not distinguish p from b. The Bakara Well Cave was found by Wayne Goedecke in the early 1970s, and the author judges that the sinkhole and gully leading to its entrance match the legend's description.

short_description.id: Chipique atau Chipekwe adalah monster air setengah ular setengah buaya dari sungai Zambezi yang membalikkan perahu.
short_description.en: The Chipique or Chipekwe is a half-snake, half-crocodile water monster of the Zambezi that overturns canoes.

long_description.id: Chipique atau Chipekwe adalah monster air legendaris setengah ular setengah buaya yang hidup di sungai Zambezi. Penduduk setempat takut kepadanya karena ia membalikkan perahu dan menyeret penumpangnya ke dasar. Para penjelajah abad ke-19 meragukan keberadaannya, dan dalam literatur Eropa ia pertama kali disebut Carl Hagenbeck pada 1909.
long_description.en: The Chipique or Chipekwe is a legendary half-snake, half-crocodile water monster of the Zambezi. Locals fear it because it overturns canoes and drags their occupants to the bottom. Nineteenth-century explorers doubted its existence, and in European literature it was first mentioned by Carl Hagenbeck in 1909.

long_description.id: Sebuah sumber lain menggambarkan seekor ular yang dikatakan hidup di kaki Air Terjun Victoria; folklor Barotse menyatakan monster ini datang dari samudra. Ia menguasai sungai pada malam hari, panjangnya tiga puluh kaki, dan dapat menyambar sampan lalu menahannya. Kepalanya kecil dan abu-abu batu tulis, tubuhnya yang berat melingkar dalam gulungan hitam. Seorang saksi mata disebut melihatnya pada 1925 menegakkan tubuh lalu menghilang ke dalam gua.
long_description.en: Another source describes a serpent said to live at the foot of Victoria Falls; Barotse folklore holds that the monster came from the ocean. It rules the river by night, is thirty feet long, and can seize a canoe and hold it fast. The head of the creature is small and slate-grey, while its heavy, serpent-like body coils in black loops. An eyewitness is said to have seen it in 1925 rear up and disappear into a cave.

long_description.id: Chōchinbi adalah jenis cahaya gaib dalam legenda Jepang. Ia muncul di atas jalan kecil di antara sawah. Cahaya itu konon menghilang ketika orang mendekat.
long_description.en: Chōchinbi is a ghost-light type in Japanese legends. It appears over footpaths between rice fields. The light is said to disappear when people approach.

long_description.id: Satu kisah dari Tokushima menggambarkan banyak cahaya yang berbaris bersama. Namanya berasal dari kemiripannya dengan lentera kertas yang dibawa orang. Satu kisah menganggap kemunculannya sebagai tanda adanya yōkai di sekitar.
long_description.en: A Tokushima account describes many lights lined up together. Its name comes from a resemblance to a carried paper lantern. One account treats its presence as a sign of nearby yōkai.

long_description.id: Ia sering muncul dalam barisan panjang berisi puluhan cahaya yang mirip untaian lentera. Namanya juga dikaitkan dengan dugaan bahwa ada makhluk yang menyalakan lentera kertas, dan cahaya itu sering disebut ulah kitsune atau, di banyak tempat, tanuki. Cirinya yang khas ialah dipakai roh-roh lain sebagai sumber cahaya.
long_description.en: It often appears in long rows of dozens of lights resembling a string of lanterns. Its name is also tied to the presumption that some creature is lighting paper lanterns, and the light is often called the work of kitsune or, in many places, tanuki. Its distinguishing feature is that other spirits use it as a light source.

long_description.id: Di Distrik Miyoshi, Prefektur Tokushima, chōchinbi disebut tanukibi dan dianggap api yang dinyalakan tanuki. Di Matsudzuka, Provinsi Yamato, api serupa disebut koemonbi; ia terutama muncul pada malam hujan di tepi sungai, sebesar lentera kertas.
long_description.en: In Miyoshi District, Tokushima Prefecture, chōchinbi are called tanukibi and are considered fires lit by tanuki. In Matsudzuka, Yamato Province, similar fires are called koemonbi; they appear mainly on rainy evenings on the river bank, about as big as a paper lantern.

summary.id: Saat kelaparan, Cikap-Kamuy meminta Gagak membawa pesan ke langit, tetapi Gagak tertidur pada hari ketiga dan dibunuhnya. Kepudang air mendengarkan dengan hormat selama enam hari, lalu membawa kabar bahwa dewa ikan dan hewan buruan marah. Cikap-Kamuy mengajari manusia ritual yang benar, dan kelaparan berakhir; karena itu gagak dan jay gunung dianggap pertanda buruk, sedangkan kepudang air pertanda baik.
summary.en: In a famine, Cikap-Kamuy asked Crow to carry a message to heaven, but Crow fell asleep on the third day and was killed. The dipper listened respectfully for six days and brought back word that the kamuy of fish and game were angry. Cikap-Kamuy taught humans the proper rituals and the famine ended; hence crows and mountain jays are ill omens and the dipper a good one.

claims.quote: Cikap-kamuy (also called Kotan-kor-kamuy, which should not be confused with Kotan-kar-kamuy) is the Ainu kamuy (god) of owls and the land.

statement.id: Cikap-kamuy adalah dewa burung hantu dan tanah dalam tradisi Ainu.
statement.en: Cikap-kamuy is an Ainu god of owls and land.

statement.id: Ia mengawasi perilaku manusia dan kamuy lainnya.
statement.en: He oversees the behavior of people and other kamuy.

claims.quote: He is considered a deity of material success.

statement.id: Ia dikaitkan dengan keberhasilan materi.
statement.en: He is associated with material success.

claims.quote: Cikap-Kamuy is depicted as a great owl, as opposed to smaller owls (such as little horned owl) that represent demons and other malicious spirits.

statement.id: Ia digambarkan sebagai burung hantu besar, berbeda dari burung hantu kecil pembawa pertanda buruk.
statement.en: He is depicted as a great owl rather than smaller ominous owls.

claims.quote: The Ainu believed that the owl watched over the mosir (country) and local kotan (villages), so Cikap-Kamuy came to be represented as the master of the domain.

statement.id: Pengawasannya atas desa memberinya peran sebagai penguasa wilayah.
statement.en: His oversight of villages gives him the role of domain master.

claims.quote: In some areas, his tears were said to be gold and silver.

statement.id: Sebagian kisah daerah menyebut air matanya menjadi emas dan perak.
statement.en: Some regional accounts make his tears gold and silver.

claims.quote: チカㇷ゚カムイは「鳥の神」の意である。その姿は偉大なシマフクロウとされている。

statement.id: Nama Cikap-kamuy (チカㇷ゚カムイ) berarti "dewa burung" (鳥の神), dan wujudnya dianggap burung hantu ikan Blakiston (シマフクロウ) yang agung.
statement.en: The name Cikap-kamuy (チカㇷ゚カムイ) means "god of birds" (鳥の神), and his form is held to be a great Blakiston’s fish owl (シマフクロウ).

claims.quote: シマフクロウと大地のカムイである。コタンコㇿカムイ（村を所有する神）ともいう。

statement.id: Ia juga disebut Kotan-kor-kamuy (コタンコㇿカムイ), "dewa pemilik desa" (村を所有する神).
statement.en: He is also called Kotan-kor-kamuy (コタンコㇿカムイ), "the god who owns the village" (村を所有する神).

claims.quote: Cikap-Kamuy wished to send a message to heaven inquiring about the cause of the famine, and he asked Crow to be his messenger.

statement.id: Ketika kelaparan melanda, Cikap-Kamuy ingin mengirim pesan ke langit untuk menanyakan sebabnya dan meminta Gagak menjadi utusannya.
statement.en: When famine struck, Cikap-Kamuy wished to send a message to heaven asking its cause, and asked Crow to be his messenger.

claims.quote: On the third day, Crow fell asleep, and Cikap-Kamuy grew angry and killed him.

statement.id: Pada hari ketiga Gagak tertidur, dan Cikap-Kamuy marah lalu membunuhnya.
statement.en: On the third day Crow fell asleep, and Cikap-Kamuy grew angry and killed him.

claims.quote: 3羽目の使者はカワガラスで、チカㇷ゚カムイが言伝をすべて伝え終わるまでの6日間、うやうやしく聞いていた。

statement.id: Utusan ketiga, burung kepudang air (カワガラス), mendengarkan dengan hormat selama 6 hari hingga Cikap-Kamuy selesai menyampaikan pesannya.
statement.en: The third messenger, the dipper (カワガラス), listened respectfully for 6 days until Cikap-Kamuy finished his message.

claims.quote: Accordingly, Cikap-Kamuy went to the humans and taught them the proper rituals to be enacted after killing a fish or a deer. Once the humans began performing these rituals, the kamuy were appeased, and the famine ceased.

statement.id: Karena dewa ikan dan hewan buruan marah, Cikap-Kamuy mengajari manusia ritual yang benar setelah membunuh ikan atau rusa; setelah ritual itu dijalankan, para kamuy reda dan kelaparan berakhir.
statement.en: Because the kamuy of fish and game were angry, Cikap-Kamuy taught humans the proper rituals after killing a fish or deer; once these were performed, the kamuy were appeased and the famine ended.

claims.quote: The Ainu considered the hondo crow and the mountain jay birds of ill omen as a result of this myth. The dipper, in contrast, was a sign of good fortune.

statement.id: Karena mitos ini, orang Ainu menganggap gagak hondo dan burung jay gunung pembawa pertanda buruk, sedangkan kepudang air (dipper) pertanda keberuntungan.
statement.en: Because of this myth, the Ainu considered the hondo crow and the mountain jay birds of ill omen, while the dipper was a sign of good fortune.

short_description.id: Clytius (Klytios) adalah salah satu raksasa Yunani yang menyerang dewa-dewa Olimpus dalam Gigantomachy. Menurut sumber-sumber kuno ia dibakar oleh obor Hekate.
short_description.en: Clytius (Klytios) is one of the Greek Giants who attacked the Olympian gods in the Gigantomachy. Ancient sources say he was burned by the torches of Hecate.

long_description.id: Clytius (Klytios) adalah salah satu raksasa mitologi Yunani yang menyerang dewa-dewa Olimpus dalam perang yang disebut Gigantomachy. Para Giants lahir dari Ge (Bumi) dengan Ouranos (Langit) sebagai ayah, tak tertandingi dalam ukuran tubuh dan tak terkalahkan oleh kekuatannya.
long_description.en: Clytius (Klytios) was one of the Giants of Greek mythology who attacked the Olympian gods in the war called the Gigantomachy. According to Pseudo-Apollodorus the Giants were born of Ge (Earth) with Ouranos (Sky) as father, vast in bodily size and beyond defeat by sheer might.

long_description.id: Dalam karya Pseudo-Apollodorus, Hekate mengalahkan Klytios dengan obor api, dan satu daftar raksasa menyebutnya sebagai Gigante yang dibakar habis oleh obor Hekate. Salah satu bacaan atas teks Apollodorus menyebut Hekate atau Hephaestus sebagai yang membakarnya dengan massa besi membara. Pada Pergamonaltar, Hekate membakarnya dengan obornya, tetapi nama lawan Hekate di sana tidak terjamin lewat prasasti dan penamaannya bertumpu pada petikan Apollodorus itu.
long_description.en: In the work of Pseudo-Apollodorus, Hekate got the better of Klytios with fire-brands, and a list of giants calls him a Gigante immolated by the torches of Hekate. One reading of the Apollodorus text names Hecate or Hephaestus as the one who burned him with glowing masses of iron. On the Pergamonaltar Hecate burns him with her torch, but the name of her opponent there is not secured by an inscription and the identification rests on that Apollodorus passage.

long_description.id: Para Giants digambarkan sebagai prajurit hoplit berzirah atau makhluk primitif berpakaian kulit binatang dengan senjata batu dan obor menyala; dalam seni patung dan mosaik mereka biasanya berekor ular. Menurut ramalan di antara para dewa, para dewa sendiri tidak dapat membinasakan satu pun dari mereka tanpa bantuan sekutu fana. Hecate dan Clytius tampil bersama pada sebuah lukisan vas figur merah Athenian (C5th B.C.).
long_description.en: The Giants were depicted as armoured hoplite warriors or as primitives clothed in animal-skins with rocks and flaming brands; in sculpture and mosaic art they usually have serpent tails. According to an oracle among the gods, the gods themselves could not destroy any of them without the help of a mortal ally. Hecate and Clytius appear together on an Athenian red-figure vase painting (C5th B.C.).

short_description.id: Damysos adalah raksasa tercepat di antara para Gigantes dalam mitologi Yunani. Menurut satu kisah, Chiron mengambil pergelangan kakinya untuk dipasang pada Achilles.
short_description.en: Damysos was the fastest of all the Giants in Greek mythology. In one account Chiron took his ankle to set into Achilles.

long_description.id: Damysos adalah raksasa tercepat dari seluruh Gigantes dalam mitologi Yunani. Para Gigantes sendiri digambarkan sebagai suku seratus raksasa kelahiran Gaia yang berperang melawan para dewa dan dibinasakan, dan satu daftar menyebut Damysos sebagai Gigante tercepat yang tewas dalam perang itu.
long_description.en: Damysos was the fastest of all the Giants in Greek mythology. The Gigantes were a tribe of a hundred giants born of Gaia who waged war on the gods and were destroyed, and one list calls Damysos the swiftest Gigante, slain in that war.

long_description.id: Menurut ringkasan Photius atas Sejarah Baru Ptolemaios Hephaistion, Chiron menggali jasad Damysos yang dimakamkan di Pallene, mengambil astragale-nya, dan memasangkannya pada kaki Achilles. Astragale itu terlepas ketika Achilles dikejar Apollon, dan Achilles pun roboh serta tewas. Para Gigantes, menurut Bibliotheca karya Pseudo-Apollodorus, lahir dari Ge dan tak tertandingi dalam ukuran tubuh maupun kekuatan.
long_description.en: According to Photius's summary of Ptolemy Hephaestion's New History, Chiron exhumed Damysos's body, buried at Pallene, took out the astragale and incorporated it into Achilles' foot. The astragale fell when Achilles was pursued by Apollon, and Achilles, fallen, was killed. The Gigantes, according to Pseudo-Apollodorus' Bibliotheca, were born of Ge and were beyond rivalry in bodily size and might.

claims.quote: DAMYSOS (Damysus) A swiftest of the Gigantes who was slain in the war against the gods. Kheiron (Chiron) exumed his body and extracting the swift "astragale" from his foot placed it in the heel of the hero Akhilleus (Achilles).

statement.id: Damysos (Damysus) adalah Gigante tercepat yang tewas dalam perang melawan para dewa; Kheiron (Chiron) menggali jasadnya, mengambil "astragale" (tulang pergelangan) yang cepat dari kakinya, lalu memasangnya pada tumit pahlawan Akhilleus (Achilles).
statement.en: Damysos (Damysus) was a swiftest of the Gigantes, slain in the war against the gods; Kheiron (Chiron) exhumed his body and took the swift "astragale" from his foot and placed it in the heel of the hero Akhilleus (Achilles).

claims.quote: Ptolemy Hephaestion, New History Book 6 (summary from Photius, Myriobiblon 190) (trans. Pearse) (Greek mythographer C1st to C2nd A.D.) : ... and confided him to Kheiron (Chiron). The latter exhumed the body of the Gigante Damysos (Damysus) who was buried at Pallene--Damysos was the fastest of all the Gigantes (Giants)--removed the astragale and incorporated it into Akhilleus' foot

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan Photius atas Sejarah Baru Ptolemaios Hephaistion, Chiron menggali jasad Gigante Damysos yang dimakamkan di Pallene, mengambil astragale-nya, dan memasangnya pada kaki Akhilleus.
statement.en: In Photius's summary of Ptolemy Hephaestion's New History, Chiron exhumed the body of the Gigante Damysos, buried at Pallene, removed the astragale and incorporated it into Akhilleus' foot.

claims.quote: Ptolemy Hephaestion, New History Book 6 (summary from Photius, Myriobiblon 190) (trans. Pearse) (Greek mythographer C1st to C2nd A.D.) : ... This astragale fell when Akhilleus was pursued by Apollon and it was thus that Akhilleus, fallen, was killed.

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan yang sama, astragale itu terlepas ketika Akhilleus dikejar Apollon, dan dengan itulah Akhilleus roboh lalu tewas.
statement.en: In the same summary, this astragale fell when Akhilleus was pursued by Apollon, and it was thus that Akhilleus, fallen, was killed.

claims.quote: THE GIGANTES were a tribe of a hundred giants born of the earth-goddess Gaia. ... At the urging of Gaia the Gigantes waged war on the gods and were destroyed in the ensuing battle.

statement.id: Para Gigantes adalah suku yang terdiri dari seratus raksasa kelahiran dewi bumi Gaia; atas dorongan Gaia mereka berperang melawan para dewa dan dibinasakan dalam pertempuran itu.
statement.en: The Gigantes were a tribe of a hundred giants born of the earth-goddess Gaia; at Gaia's urging they waged war on the gods and were destroyed in the ensuing battle.

claims.quote: Pseudo-Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 1. 34 - 38 (trans. Aldrich) (Greek mythographer C2nd A.D.) : ... Ge (Gaea, the Earth) gave birth to the Gigantes (Giants), Ouranos (Uranus, Sky) was the father. These creatures were unsurpassed in the size of their bodies and unconquerable by virtue of their power.

statement.id: Dalam Bibliotheca karya Pseudo-Apollodorus, Ge (Bumi) melahirkan para Gigantes (Giants) dengan Ouranos (Langit) sebagai ayah; mereka tak tertandingi dalam ukuran tubuh dan tak terkalahkan oleh kekuatannya.
statement.en: In Pseudo-Apollodorus, Bibliotheca, Ge (Earth) gave birth to the Gigantes (Giants), with Ouranos (Sky) as father; they were unsurpassed in the size of their bodies and unconquerable by virtue of their power.

short_description.id: Dokkakgwi adalah makhluk berkaki satu dalam cerita rakyat Asia Timur, terutama dikaitkan dengan dokkaebi Korea.
short_description.en: Dokkakgwi is a one-legged East Asian folkloric being particularly linked to Korean dokkaebi.

long_description.id: Dokkakgwi adalah makhluk berkaki satu dalam cerita rakyat Asia Timur, terutama dikaitkan dengan dokkaebi Korea. Dokkakgwi adalah salah satu bentuk dokkaebi, yang dapat berasal dari benda mati berjiwa. Dokkaebi juga disebut dengan nama-nama seperti dokkakgwi, dan kepercayaan dokkaebi diperkirakan sudah ada sejak zaman Tiga Kerajaan.
long_description.en: Dokkakgwi is a one-legged East Asian folkloric being particularly linked to Korean dokkaebi. Dokkakgwi is one form of dokkaebi, which may arise from spirit-bearing inanimate objects. Dokkaebi are also called by names such as dokkakgwi, and dokkaebi belief is presumed to have existed already in the Three Kingdoms period.

long_description.id: Dokkaebi yang berwujud dikisahkan berambut kusut dan berkaki satu sehingga berjalan dengan melompat-lompat; kaki tunggal itu dikatakan hitam seperti dilapisi pernis, dan Baopuzi juga mencatat bahwa dokkaebi hanya berkaki satu. Berbeda dari hantu yang berasal dari roh orang mati, dokkaebi dikatakan terjadi dari benda alam seperti pohon dan batu. Mereka dikatakan dapat menjadi tak kasatmata dan menunjukkan kekuatan luar biasa, serta sangat gemar berbuat usil.
long_description.en: Dokkaebi that have a form are told of as having disheveled hair and one leg, so they hop about; the single leg is said to be black as if lacquered, and the Baopuzi also records that dokkaebi have only one foot. Unlike ghosts that come from the souls of the dead, dokkaebi are said to arise from natural objects such as trees and stones. They are said to be able to become invisible and to show superhuman strength, and they greatly enjoy mischievous pranks.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah dongeng, seorang pemuda bertemu dokkaebi yang menantangnya bergulat dan menang berkali-kali karena dokkaebi hanya berkaki satu. Tradisi makhluk berkaki satu Tiongkok dianggap mungkin memengaruhi tradisi Korea berikutnya. Dalam perkembangan sesudah Enam Dinasti, makhluk ini juga dikaitkan dengan kekayaan dan keberuntungan.
long_description.en: In one folktale, a young man meets a dokkaebi that challenges him to wrestle and wins repeatedly because the dokkaebi has only one leg. Chinese one-legged-being traditions are considered possible influences on later Korean traditions. In developments after the Six Dynasties, the being was also associated with wealth and fortune.

claims.quote: Dujiaogui (Chinese: 独脚鬼; pinyin: Dújiǎoguǐ) or dokkakgwi (Korean: 독각귀; Hanja: 獨脚鬼), literally "One-Legged Ghost" or "One-Legged Demon", is a legendary creature found in East Asian folklore. The creature appears in Chinese folklore, but the one-legged form is particularly associated with Korean folklore, where it is described as a type of dokkaebi.

statement.id: Dokkakgwi adalah makhluk berkaki satu dalam cerita rakyat Asia Timur, terutama dikaitkan dengan dokkaebi Korea.
statement.en: Dokkakgwi is a one-legged East Asian folkloric being particularly linked to Korean dokkaebi.

claims.quote: Unlike ghosts (gwisin), which are believed to be the souls of the dead, dokkaebi are supernatural beings associated with inanimate objects that have acquired a spirit, including old brooms, inkstones, and household tools stained with human blood. The one-legged dokkakgwi is one form of the dokkaebi.

statement.id: Dokkakgwi adalah salah satu bentuk dokkaebi, yang dapat berasal dari benda mati berjiwa.
statement.en: Dokkakgwi is one form of dokkaebi, which may arise from spirit-bearing inanimate objects.

claims.quote: One-legged supernatural beings appear in early Chinese mythology and may have influenced later Korean traditions. The Chinese classic Classic of Mountains and Seas (Shanhaijing) describes a one-legged mountain spirit or beast called Kui (夔). In southern China, the Wutong Shen (五通神) was also known as the "One-legged Wutong" (独脚五通).

statement.id: Tradisi makhluk berkaki satu Tiongkok dianggap mungkin memengaruhi tradisi Korea berikutnya.
statement.en: Chinese one-legged-being traditions are considered possible influences on later Korean traditions.

claims.quote: After the Six dynasties period, the figure developed other characteristics. It came to be associated with wealth and good fortune, as well as with a lecherous monster that attacked women. One explanation attributes these changes to the southward migration of the Han people and its influence on the beliefs of ethnic minorities.

statement.id: Dalam perkembangan sesudah Enam Dinasti, makhluk ini juga dikaitkan dengan kekayaan dan keberuntungan.
statement.en: In developments after the Six Dynasties, the being was also associated with wealth and fortune.

claims.quote: 도채비·독각귀(獨脚鬼)·독갑이［狐魅］·허주(虛主)·허체(虛體)·망량(魍魎)·영감(제주도) 등의 이름으로 불리기도 한다. ≪삼국유사≫ 등 여러 문헌에도 기록되어 있는 것을 볼 때 삼국시대도 이미 도깨비신앙이 존재하고 있었다고 추측된다.

statement.id: Dokkaebi juga disebut dengan nama-nama seperti dokkakgwi (독각귀, 獨脚鬼); dari catatan dalam sejumlah naskah seperti Samguk Yusa (삼국유사), kepercayaan dokkaebi diperkirakan sudah ada sejak zaman Tiga Kerajaan (삼국시대).
statement.en: Dokkaebi are also called by names such as dokkakgwi (독각귀, 獨脚鬼); from records in several texts such as the Samguk Yusa (삼국유사), dokkaebi belief is presumed to have existed already in the Three Kingdoms period (삼국시대).

claims.quote: 형체가 있는 도깨비의 모습은 머리를 산발하고 다닌다든지, 다리가 하나밖에 없어서 껑충껑충 뛰어다닌다든지, 키가 커서 하늘까지 닿고 머리가 구름 위에 솟아 있다고 전해져 내려온다.

statement.id: Dokkaebi yang berwujud dikisahkan berambut kusut, berkaki satu sehingga berjalan dengan melompat-lompat, atau sangat tinggi hingga menyentuh langit dengan kepala menjulang di atas awan.
statement.en: Dokkaebi that have a form are told of as having disheveled hair, having only one leg and so hopping about, or being so tall they touch the sky with their heads above the clouds.

claims.quote: 하나밖에 없는 다리는 옻칠한 것같이 검으며, 키가 너무 커서 옷을 못 해 입고 백지로 가릴 곳만 가리고 있다고도 한다. ≪포박자 抱朴子≫에도 도깨비는 발이 하나밖에 없다고 기록된 것을 볼 때 도깨비의 발이 하나라는 이야기는 고대부터 동양에 널리 퍼진 것임을 알 수 있다.

statement.id: Kaki tunggal dokkaebi dikatakan hitam seperti dilapisi pernis; karena Baopuzi (포박자, 抱朴子) juga mencatat bahwa dokkaebi hanya berkaki satu, cerita tentang kaki tunggal itu dinilai telah tersebar luas di Timur (동양) sejak zaman kuno.
statement.en: The single leg of the dokkaebi is said to be black as if lacquered; because the Baopuzi (포박자, 抱朴子) also records that dokkaebi have only one foot, the story of the one foot is judged to have been widespread in the East (동양) since ancient times.

claims.quote: 옛날 한 젊은이가 장에 갔다오는 길에 도깨비를 만났다. 도깨비는 젊은이에게 씨름을 하자고 청하였고 젊은이는 도깨비와 여러 번 씨름을 해서 이겼다. 도깨비는 계속해서 대들었지만 다리가 하나밖에 없었으므로 젊은이는 다리를 감아 쉽게 넘어뜨릴 수 있었다는 이야기이다.

short_description.id: Döö adalah raksasa bermata satu dalam dongeng rakyat Kirgiz: makhluk berwujud manusia sebesar gunung yang kuat luar biasa tetapi bodoh, sehingga dalam hampir semua cerita ia dikalahkan manusia.
short_description.en: Döö is a one-eyed giant of Kyrgyz folk tales: a human-shaped being as big as a mountain, immensely strong but dim-witted, so that in almost every story it is defeated by a human.

long_description.id: Dalam dongeng rakyat Kirgiz, Döö adalah tokoh negatif berupa raksasa mitologis. Ia berwujud dan berbicara seperti manusia, tetapi tubuhnya sebesar gunung dan cambuknya sebesar pohon. Di dahinya hanya ada satu mata; ia bergerak di bawah maupun di atas tanah, sekali makan menghabiskan bekal beberapa hari, dan tidur berminggu-minggu dengan satu telinga sebagai alas dan telinga lain sebagai selimut.
long_description.en: In Kyrgyz folk tales Döö is a negative character in the form of a mythological giant. It looks and speaks like a human, but its body is as large as a mountain and its whip as big as a tree. It has a single eye on its forehead, moves both under and above the ground, eats several days' food in one meal, and sleeps for weeks with one ear as a mattress and the other as a blanket.

long_description.id: Artikel kedua menambahkan bahwa döö bermata satu tampak menakutkan, sebagian berkepala banyak, berbulu di seluruh tubuh, dan memiliki kekuatan sihir. Mereka biasa tinggal di gua-gua gunung yang terpencil, di hutan lebat, atau menguasai negeri tertentu; mereka memakan daging manusia dan tidak memakai senjata.
long_description.en: The second article adds that one-eyed döös look terrifying, some have several heads, their bodies are covered in hair, and they possess magical power. They usually live in remote mountain caves or dense forests, or rule over particular lands; they eat human flesh and do not use weapons.

long_description.id: Kekuatannya tak terbatas dan ia tidak mudah dibunuh, tetapi kecerdasannya rendah, sehingga dalam hampir semua alur cerita ia kalah oleh manusia. Menurut artikel kedua, selain penguasa gunung, döö juga dipandang sebagai roh penguasa penyakit dan kematian.
long_description.en: Its strength is boundless and it is hard to kill, but its intelligence is limited, so in almost every plot it is beaten by a human. According to the second article, besides being master of the mountain, the döö is also regarded as the spirit ruling illness and death.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi bangsa-bangsa Sayan-Altai, Döö dikenal sebagai utusan dunia orang mati di atas bumi. Artikel kedua berpendapat bahwa citra ini masuk ke folklor Kirgiz melalui pengaruh bangsa-bangsa tetangga, dan bahwa kisah tentang raksasa bermata satu tersebar luas dalam folklor Turk-Mongol.
long_description.en: In the mythology of the Sayan-Altai peoples, Döö is known as the above-ground messenger of the world of the dead. The second article holds that this image entered Kyrgyz folklore through the influence of neighbouring peoples, and that tales of one-eyed giants are widespread in Turkic-Mongol folklore.

who.id: Döö adalah raksasa bermata satu dalam dongeng rakyat Kirgiz.
who.en: Döö is a one-eyed giant of Kyrgyz folk tales.

origin.id: Ia tokoh negatif dalam dongeng rakyat Kirgiz dan dikenal pula dalam mitologi Sayan-Altai.
origin.en: It is a negative character in Kyrgyz folk tales and is also known in Sayan-Altai mythology.

role.id: Ia menjadi lawan manusia yang kuat tetapi bodoh.
role.en: It serves as a strong but foolish opponent of humans.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal karena tidur berbulan-bulan beralaskan satu telinga dan berselimut telinga lainnya.
famous_for.en: It is known for sleeping for months on one ear while covered by the other.

did_you_know.id: Döö konon bisa menghabiskan makanan untuk beberapa hari dalam sekali makan.
did_you_know.en: Döö is said to eat several days' worth of food in a single meal.

description.id: Ia berukuran sangat besar dan memiliki kekuatan kasar tanpa batas.
description.en: It is huge and has boundless brute strength.

description.id: Döö bermata satu disebut memiliki kekuatan sihir.
description.en: One-eyed döös are said to have magical power.

description.id: Kecerdasannya terbatas, sehingga dalam hampir semua cerita ia dikalahkan manusia.
description.en: Its intelligence is limited, so in almost every story it is defeated by humans.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa raksasa dalam banyak dongeng digambarkan kuat tetapi mudah diakali?
learning_questions.en: Why are giants in many folk tales shown as strong but easy to outwit?

claims.quote: Дөө — кыргыз элинин жөө жомокторундагы терс каармандын образы.

statement.id: Döö (Дөө) adalah citra tokoh negatif (терс каарман) dalam dongeng rakyat Kirgiz (кыргыз элинин жөө жомокторундагы).
statement.en: Döö (Дөө) is the image of a negative character (терс каармандын образы) in the folk tales of the Kyrgyz people (кыргыз элинин жөө жомокторундагы).

claims.quote: Дөө - адам кейпиндеги, адамча сүйлөгөн, аябагандай зор, көлөмү тоодой, камчысы карагайдай мифологиялык алп.

statement.id: Döö adalah raksasa mitologis (мифологиялык алп) berwujud manusia yang berbicara seperti manusia, sangat besar, seukuran gunung, dengan cambuk sebesar pohon pinus.
statement.en: Döö is a mythological giant (мифологиялык алп) of human form who speaks like a human, enormous, the size of a mountain (көлөмү тоодой), with a whip like a spruce tree (камчысы карагайдай).

claims.quote: Маңдайында жалгыз көзү бар, жер астында же үстүндө жүрүп, бир нече күндүн тамагын бир эле жеп коёт.

statement.id: Ia memiliki satu mata di dahi (маңдайында жалгыз көзү), berjalan di bawah atau di atas tanah, dan sekali makan menghabiskan makanan untuk beberapa hari.
statement.en: It has a single eye on its forehead (маңдайында жалгыз көзү), goes about under or above the ground, and eats several days' worth of food at once.

claims.quote: Бир кулагын төшөнүп, экинчисин жамынып, ойлонбостон жумалап, айлап уйкуга кетет.

statement.id: Ia tidur berminggu-minggu bahkan berbulan-bulan, beralaskan satu telinga dan berselimutkan telinga yang lain.
statement.en: It sleeps for weeks and months (жумалап, айлап уйкуга кетет), lying on one ear and covering itself with the other (бир кулагын төшөнүп, экинчисин жамынып).

claims.quote: Дөө дээрлик бардык сюжеттерде адамдан акылсыз болуп, жеңилет.

statement.id: Dalam hampir semua alur cerita, Döö lebih bodoh daripada manusia dan dikalahkan.
statement.en: In almost all plots (дээрлик бардык сюжеттерде) Döö is less clever than a human (адамдан акылсыз) and is defeated (жеңилет).

claims.quote: Дөө Саян-Алтай элдеринин мифологиясында жер астындагы өлүктөр дүйнөсүнүн (Улген) жер үстүндөгү чабарманы катары белгилүү.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi bangsa-bangsa Sayan-Altai, Döö dikenal sebagai utusan di atas bumi dari dunia orang mati di bawah tanah (Улген).
statement.en: In the mythology of the Sayan-Altai peoples (Саян-Алтай элдеринин) Döö is known as the above-ground messenger (чабарман) of the underground world of the dead (жер астындагы өлүктөр дүйнөсү, Улген).

claims.quote: Жалгыз көздүү дөөлөр негизинен адамдарга окшошуп турса да, алардан өзгөчөлөнүп кебетеси коркунучтуу, кай биринин бир нече башы болот. Дөөнүн тулкусун бүтүндөй жүн баскан. Алардын сыйкырчылык касиети да бар.

statement.id: Dөө bermata satu pada dasarnya mirip manusia tetapi berpenampilan menakutkan, sebagian berkepala banyak; tubuhnya seluruhnya berbulu dan mereka memiliki kemampuan sihir (сыйкырчылык касиети).
statement.en: One-eyed döös (жалгыз көздүү дөөлөр) basically resemble humans but look terrifying, some have several heads (бир нече башы); the döö's body is entirely covered in hair (жүн), and they have magical power (сыйкырчылык касиети).

claims.quote: Көп учурларда Дөөлөр түнт токойлордо, коркунучтуу үңкүрлөрдө, кээде белгилүү бир өлкөлөрдө бийлик жүргүзөт.

statement.id: Sering kali para Döö berkuasa di hutan lebat, gua-gua menakutkan, dan kadang di negeri-negeri tertentu.
statement.en: Often Döös hold sway in dense forests (түнт токойлордо), frightening caves (коркунучтуу үңкүрлөрдө), and sometimes in particular lands.

claims.quote: адатта дөөлөр адам баласы көп жүрбөгөн, жолу татаал, же алыс жерлердеги тоонун үңкүрүндө жашашат, киши этин жейт, курал пайдаланбайт

statement.id: Biasanya para döö tinggal di gua-gua gunung di tempat jauh yang jarang didatangi manusia dan sulit dicapai, memakan daging manusia, dan tidak memakai senjata.
statement.en: Usually döös live in mountain caves (тоонун үңкүрүндө) in remote, hard-to-reach places rarely visited by people, eat human flesh (киши этин жейт) and do not use weapons (курал пайдаланбайт).

claims.quote: Өзгөчө чоң көлөмгө жана чексиз кара күчкө ээ, бирок акыл деңгээли чектелген, алар оңойлук менен өлбөйт.

statement.id: Mereka berukuran sangat besar dan memiliki kekuatan kasar tanpa batas, tetapi kecerdasannya terbatas, dan mereka tidak mudah mati.
statement.en: They are of especially great size and have boundless brute strength (чексиз кара күчкө ээ), but limited intelligence (акыл деңгээли чектелген), and they do not die easily (оңойлук менен өлбөйт).

claims.quote: Д-лөр тоонун ээси болуудан башка оорунун, өлүм-житимдин да ээси — духу.

statement.id: Selain sebagai penguasa gunung, para Döö juga penguasa, yakni roh, penyakit dan kematian.
statement.en: Besides being masters of the mountain (тоонун ээси), Döös are also the masters, the spirits (духу), of illness and death (оорунун, өлүм-житимдин).

claims.quote: Ушул чөлкөмдө жашаган элдердин таасири, карым-катнашы аркылуу мифологиялык бул образ кыргыз фольклоруна киргендиги шексиз.

statement.id: Citra mitologis ini dipastikan masuk ke folklor Kirgiz melalui pengaruh dan hubungan dengan bangsa-bangsa yang tinggal di kawasan tersebut.
statement.en: This mythological image undoubtedly entered Kyrgyz folklore (кыргыз фольклоруна) through the influence of and contacts with the peoples living in that region (ушул чөлкөмдө жашаган элдердин).

claims.quote: Мындай сюжет түрк-моңгол фольклорунда кеңири кездешет.

statement.id: Alur cerita semacam ini banyak dijumpai dalam folklor Turk-Mongol (түрк-моңгол фольклорунда).
statement.en: Such a plot is widely found in Turkic-Mongol folklore (түрк-моңгол фольклорунда).

gaps.searched: Kedua artikel ky tidak menyebut negara modern atau periode pencatatan.

Kedua sumber adalah artikel Wikipedia bahasa Kirgiz (berbasis kamus etnografi dan ensiklopedia Manas); PDF ensiklopedia Manas yang ditemukan terlalu besar untuk dikutip dengan andal, sehingga tidak dipakai.
Artikel kedua membandingkan döö dengan kisah raksasa bermata satu di tradisi lain, tetapi nama-nama itu berada dalam kalimat bertanda kutip sehingga tidak dikutip.
Tidak ditemukan berkas Commons yang menggambarkan Döö.

short_description.id: Dot adalah roh jahat penghuni air dalam kepercayaan rakyat yang dijelaskan artikel Assam.
short_description.en: Dot is an aquatic evil spirit in the folk belief described by the Assamese article.

long_description.id: Dot adalah roh jahat penghuni air dalam kepercayaan rakyat yang dijelaskan artikel Assam. Ia memperdaya manusia dan membuat mereka tersesat.
long_description.en: Dot is an aquatic evil spirit in the folk belief described by the Assamese article. It deceives people and makes them lose their way.

long_description.id: Ia dapat muncul sebagai orang yang dikenal lalu membawa korban ke kolam. Tempat tinggalnya dikatakan berada di saluran air, kolam, atau rawa. Ia memiliki kantong atau jaring yang, jika dikuasai manusia, membuatnya menaati perintah.
long_description.en: It may appear as a familiar person and lead a victim toward a pond. Its dwelling is said to lie in channels, ponds or marshes. It has a bag or net which, if controlled by a person, makes it obey commands.

long_description.id: Dalam bukunya tentang roh-roh Assam, Rajkhowa menyebut kata dot berasal dari kata Sanskerta daitya. Dot digambarkan ramping tetapi tinggi, sekitar 18 kaki, berjari panjang seperti paku, dan tinggal di parit, kolam, serta rawa. Ia meringkik seperti kuda dan tidak berdaya mendekati orang saleh; bila jimat ajaibnya hilang, ia kehilangan semua kekuatan dan menjadi pelayan terikat bagi manusia.
long_description.en: In his book on Assamese spirits, Rajkhowa says the word dot is derived from the Sanskrit daitya. The dot is described as slender but tall, about 18 feet, with long fingers like spikes, living in channels, tanks and morasses. It neighs like a horse and is powerless to approach a righteous man; if it is bereft of its wonderful talisman, it loses all powers and becomes a bound servant to the man.

short_description.id: Dungarvon Whooper adalah kisah hantu dari New Brunswick, Kanada, tentang arwah seorang juru masak kamp penebang kayu yang dibunuh di tepi Sungai Dungarvon dan menjerit di malam hari.
short_description.en: The Dungarvon Whooper is a ghost story from New Brunswick, Canada, about the spirit of a lumber-camp cook murdered along the Dungarvon River who is said to cry out at night.

long_description.id: Dungarvon Whooper (dibaca "hooper") adalah kisah hantu yang diceritakan dalam sebuah lagu karya Michael Whelan tentang dugaan pembunuhan di tepi Sungai Dungarvon di tengah New Brunswick, Kanada, pada pertengahan hingga akhir abad ke-19. Asal-usul pastinya tidak diketahui, tetapi versi paling terkenal berasal dari lagu Whelan yang dimuat di surat kabar lokal pada 1912.
long_description.en: Dungarvon Whooper (the name is pronounced "hooper") is a spectral tale carried in a song written by Michael Whelan, concerning a supposed killing on the Dungarvon River in central New Brunswick, Canada, between the middle and end of the 19th century. Nobody knows exactly where it began, but the best-known telling is Whelan's song, printed in a local paper in 1912.

long_description.id: Kisah itu berkisar pada seorang juru masak muda di kamp penebang kayu di tepi Sungai Dungarvon. Saat para penebang pergi, ia ditinggal berdua dengan bos kamp, yang memutuskan membunuh dan merampoknya. Malam itu suara "whooping" yang mengerikan membuat rombongan tak bisa tidur, diduga hantu korban yang menjerit menentang kejahatan itu; para lelaki melarikan diri, dan akhirnya seorang pastor datang dan doanya menenangkan arwah itu.
long_description.en: The story revolves around a young cook in a lumber camp on the Dungarvon River. While the lumberjacks are away, he is left alone with the camp boss, who decides to murder and rob him. That night a terrible "whooping" sound keeps the group awake, presumably the victim's ghost crying out against the crime; the men flee, and finally a priest arrives and his prayers bring peace to the spirit.

long_description.id: Dalam kebanyakan versi, sang juru masak dianggap orang Irlandia dan diberi nama Ryan atau Ryan Garvon; peristiwa itu konon terjadi sekitar 1850–1875, masa migrasi besar dari Irlandia ke Kanada setelah Kelaparan Besar. Wujud Whooper biasanya berupa hantu tak terlihat, tetapi kadang disebut menyerupai makhluk mirip kucing liar atau puma. Ada komentar bahwa panggilan "whooping" itu mungkin sebenarnya berasal dari burung hantu screech owl atau panther.
long_description.en: Most tellings make the cook an Irishman, and later versions name him Ryan or Ryan Garvon; the events are placed around 1850–1875, an era when many people migrated from Ireland to Canada after the Great Famine. The Whooper is usually described as an invisible ghost, though some say it looks like a wildcat or puma-like animal. Some commentators suggest the "whooping" may really have been a screech owl or a panther.

long_description.id: Penceritaan ulang oleh S. E. Schlosser berbeda: seorang penebang kayu Irlandia bernama Ryan menembak mati sang juru masak di hutan demi uangnya; setiap senja selama beberapa minggu hantu sang juru masak menjerit, dan seorang pastor yang mencoba mengusirnya dengan lonceng, kitab, dan lilin pergi dalam kekalahan. Seorang penutur dari Maine, Leroy Dudley, menceritakan versi saat Dungarvon Whooper memperebutkan kekuasaan atas Katahdin dengan roh pribumi Amerika Pamola.
long_description.en: A retelling by S. E. Schlosser differs: an Irish lumberjack named Ryan shoots the cook dead in the woods for his money; every dusk for several weeks the cook's ghost shrieks, and a priest who tries to exorcise it with bell, book and candle leaves in defeat. A Maine storyteller, Leroy Dudley, tells a version in which the Dungarvon Whooper contests the Native American spirit Pamola for hegemony over Katahdin.
